### [2027 OFFICIAL RULE / CLARIFICATION: Verified 2027 Official Rules & National Clarifications Baseline (As of 2026-11-22) { **[S01,S02,S03,S04,S05,S06]**}]

- **Governing Sources Verified:** Licensed 2027 Division C Rules Manual (*Thermodynamics C*, pp. C57–C59; *General Rules*, p. C1; *Calculators*, p. C74; *Eye Protection*, p. C75; *Schedule*, p. C78)  **[S01]**, all **9** Official 2027 National Rules Clarifications (`09/30/2026`–`10/28/2026`)  **[S02]**, **0** Official Rules Corrections  **[S03]**, Official Team Checklist (`10/20/2026`) & v2.0.0 Scoresheet (`11/06/2026`)  **[S04]**, and Official 2027 Event Supervisor Testing Guide  **[S05]**.
- **Format & Permitted Resources (**[2027-RULE]** 1, 2.a–e):** Hybrid event | Up to **2 competitors** | **50 min** | **Impound: Yes** (ONLY pre-built device & spare parts at room temp; non-impound incurs $\times 0.7$ construction violation  **[S02]**) | **Eye Protection: None required** | Up to **two Class III calculators** (**[2027-RULE]** 2.b) | **Unrestricted paper notes/binders of any size from any source; pages MAY be separated or removed during any part of the event (**[2027-RULE]** 2.c)** | Setup tools & prepared prediction graphs/tables permitted and NOT impounded (**[2027-RULE]** 2.d).
- **2027 Heat-Lamp Collector Task (**[2027-RULE]** 3.a–h, 4.a–g, 5.II.a–i):** Passive device inside a $\mathbf{30.0\text{ **cm**}\times 30.0\text{ **cm**}\times 30.0\text{ **cm**}}$ cube collects radiant/convective heat from an ES-provided clamp lamp with metal reflector and $\mathbf{100\text{--}125\text{ **W**}}$ **untinted incandescent heat lamp bulb** (no LED, halogen, or ceramic) mounted at bottom-of-bulb height $h_{\mathrm{bulb}} \in [40 cm,50 cm]$ (**Regionals**, $5 cm$ steps), $[40 cm,55 cm]$ (**States**, $5 cm$ steps), or $[40 cm,65 cm]$ (**Nationals**, $1 cm$ steps) to warm $\mathbf{100\text{ **mL**}}$ room-temp water in an ES-provided **9 oz clear plastic party cup** ($\approx9.9–10.2 cm$ tall, $\approx7.4–7.6 cm$ mouth) over $t_{\mathrm{heat}} = 10 min$ (**Regionals**) or $10–15 min$ (**States/Nationals**, $1 min$ steps).
- **Critical Construction & Operating Bans:** (**1**) **BANNED HAZARDOUS MATERIALS (**[2027-RULE]** 3.b.i, 3.b.iii & Clarif. #6):** Asbestos, mineral wool, fiberglass, and **polystyrene / Styrofoam / #6 PS plastic** $\to$ **device disqualified from setup/testing ($\mathrm{TS}=\mathrm{PS}=0$)**. (**2**) No commercial thermoses/coolers/vacuum vessels, thermometers/probes, or electrical/chemical energy sources (**[2027-RULE]** 3.b.ii, 3.f). (**3**) Internal overhang inside cup is allowed, but **zero device contact with water and zero water additives (**[2027-RULE]** 3.e)**. (**4**) **No stirring, swirling, or shaking by team or ES; ES measures top water layer near center ( **[S02]** Clarif. #1–#4)**. (**5**) Unattached foil/film wrap may rest on cup if zero tape/adhesives/clips attach to cup and all wrap is removed before final measurement ( **[S02]** Clarif. #5).
- **Written Test Scope (**[2027-RULE]** 5.I.a–d) & Scoring (**[2027-RULE]** 6.a–j):** Minimum 3 questions per area: **5.c.i** Foundations/Zeroth Law/Scales/Units; **5.c.ii** Phases/Diagrams/Latent Heat/Gas Laws; **5.c.iii** Heat Transfer/Conductivity/Specific Heat; **5.c.iv** Processes/Cycles/Engines/1st & 2nd Laws; **5.c.v** History of **Kelvin, Black, Joule, Carnot, Planck, Clausius, Boltzmann, Maxwell**; **5.c.vi** **[STATE/NAT]** Blackbody/Stefan–Boltzmann/3rd Law; **5.c.vii** **[STATE/NAT]** Entropy & Enthalpy. **Rule 5.d.iv:** *No questions may require trigonometry or calculus.*
  
$$
\mathrm{FS} = \mathrm{ES}_{50} + \mathrm{TS}_{30} + \mathrm{PS}_{20}\ (\le 100),\quad
    \mathrm{TG} = T_f - T_i,\quad
    \mathrm{PE} = 1 - \frac{|T_f - T_{\mathrm{pred}}|}{T_f}\ (\text{in }^\circ\mathrm{C},\ \ge 0),\quad
    \text{Penalties: }\times 0.7^{N_{\mathrm{constr}}}\times 0.9^{N_{\mathrm{comp}}}.
$$

  **Tiebreakers (**[2027-RULE]** 6.j):** **1st:** Best $\mathrm{TS}$ | **2nd:** Best $\mathrm{ES}$ | **3rd:** Preselected written test questions.

# §0: Competition Command Center {#sec:00}

> **[SCOPE: REQUIRED | 2027 Rules 1, 2.a–e, 3.a–h, 4.a–g, 5.I–II, 6.a–j & Official National Clarifications #1–#9]**

## 2027 Official Rules Snapshot & Paradigm-Shift Mandate

### [2027 OFFICIAL RULE / CLARIFICATION: 2026–2027 Division C Thermodynamics Official Event Profile { **[S01,S02,S03,S04,S05]**}]
- **Event Type & Header ( **[S01]** pp. C2, C57):** **Hybrid Event** (Written Test + Pre-Built Heat-Collecting Device) | **Team Size:** Up to **2** students | **Approx. Time:** **50 min** | **Impound:** **Yes** (*only* device and spare parts, at room temperature per Rule `2.d`) | **Calculator:** Up to **two Class III** programmable/graphing calculators (`2.b`, p. C74) | **Eye Protection:** **None required** (header & Checklist  **[S04]**; water is non-hazardous per p. C75).
- **Unrestricted Removable Paper Notes (`2.c`):** Teams may bring paper notes/resources of **any size**, in any form and from any source (binders, books, notebooks, folders, sheet protectors, lamination, tabs, labels permitted). **Competitors may separate or remove pages from containers for use during any part of the event.** Notes, prepared calculation graphs/tables (`2.d`), setup tools (`2.d`), calculators (`2.b`), and writing utensils (`2.a`) are **NOT impounded**.
- **CRITICAL 2027 PARADIGM SHIFT (`1`, `3.a`, `4.a–g`):** Unlike 2018–2019 (insulating box holding a pre-heated beaker of hot water with a 10-pt Plot Score), the **2027 device is an optical/thermal heat collector** placed under an Event Supervisor-provided **100–125 W untinted incandescent/IR heat lamp bulb** (mounted facing straight down at height $h_{\mathrm{bulb}} = 40–65 cm$ above the Testing Surface) for $t_{\mathrm{heat}} = 10–15 min$ to heat **100 mL of room-temperature water** in an ES-provided **9 oz clear plastic disposable party cup** ($\approx 3.9\text{--}4.0\text{ in}$ [9.9–10.2 cm] tall, $\approx 2.9\text{--}3.0\text{ in}$ [7.4–7.6 cm] mouth) inside a **$30.0 cm \times 30.0 cm \times 30.0 cm$ cube** (`3.d`). The Plot Score is eliminated: $\mathrm{FS} = \mathrm{ES\,(50)} + \mathrm{TS\,(30)} + \mathrm{PS\,(20)}$.

**Official 2027 National Rules Corrections & Clarifications Ledger (Verified `2026-11-22`  **[S02,S03]**).**
As of `2026-11-22`, the official corrections page (`soinc.org/events/rules-corrections`) lists **0 Rules Corrections** for Thermodynamics B/C  **[S03]**, while the clarifications portal (`soinc.org/division-c-events`) publishes **9 binding Official National Rule Clarifications**  **[S02]** (General Rule 3, p. C1):

| **# / Date** | **Clause** | **Official Ruling Summary **[S02]**** | **Direct Engineering & Execution Mandate** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **C1** `09/30/26` | `5.II.g` L4 | Water **will not be stirred or swirled** before taking temperature. | Overhead near-IR radiation creates strong vertical thermal stratification ($T_{\mathrm{top}} > T_{\mathrm{bulk}}$); calibrate prediction tables for **unstirred** water (§`sec:15`, §`sec:16`). |
| **C2** `10/01/26` | `5.II.g` L1 | Students may **not swish water around** in cup prior to measurement. | Lift cup vertically with zero sloshing during the 1-min removal window so the hot top layer does not mix with cooler bottom water. |
| **C3** `10/06/26` | `5.II.g` L2 | Team **must not swirl, shake, or stir** cup during removal. | Swishing/shaking violates competition rules ($\times 0.9$ penalty) *and* lowers measured $T_f$ by $1.5–4.0 °C$, hurting $\mathrm{TS}$. |
| **C4** `10/06/26` | `5.II.g` L4 | Local ES sets uniform protocol; National recommendation is measuring **top layer of water near center of cup** (probe inserted just far enough for accurate reading). | Confirmed in Official ES Guide **[S05]**: probe tip sits in the upper central water layer ($\sim5–10 mm$ depth). Maximize top-surface IR absorption and suppress top-surface evaporation! |
| **C5** `10/21/26` | `5.II.d` L2 | Teams **may place something on/around cup** during Water Setup, provided **no adhesives, tapes, or fasteners (rubber bands, clips)** attach to cup and cup shape/integrity is unaltered. | Use a gravity-resting clear BoPET film evaporation cover or loose reflector collar resting on the rim with **zero tape/clips**, zero water contact (`3.e`), and strip it completely off before $T_f$ measurement (`5.II.g`). |
| **C6** `10/22/26` | `3.b.i` L1 | **Polystyrene (Styrofoam & plastics with recycling symbol `#6` / `PS`) is hazardous under a heat lamp and prohibited.** | **HARD DISQUALIFICATION FROM PART II (`3.b.iii`):** Any Styrofoam (EPS/XPS) or `#6 PS` bars the device from setup/testing ($\mathrm{TS}=\mathrm{PS}=0$). Use cork, cardboard, balsa, cotton, wool, or foil air-gaps (§`sec:14`). |
| **C7** `10/22/26` | `5.II.b` L5.2 | Lifting/opening a reflector lid to place the cup underneath and returning lid to original position is allowed. | Hinged or pin-aligned top reflector cone lids that lift open during 1-min Water Setup Time are $100\%$ legal under `5.II.b`. |
| **C8** `10/22/26` | `5.II.b` L4 | Opening/closing a lid/door or shifting device position/orientation inherent to inserting the cup is **not** “modifying” the device. | Sliding the device out to load the cup and recentering it under the switched-off lamp during 1-min Water Setup Time incurs zero penalty. |
| **C9** `10/28/26` | `2.d` L1 | **Devices not impounded incur one additional construction violation.** | Matched in Scoresheet v2.0.0 (`11/06/26` **[S04]**): missing impound multiplies $\mathrm{TS}$ and $\mathrm{PS}$ by $0.7\times$. Always impound device + spares on time! |

## 2027 Scoring Engine, Penalty Stacking & Tiebreaker Mathematics

### [FORMULA & DECISION CARD: Official 2027 Scoring Equations, Penalty Multipliers & Tiebreakers (Rule 6.a–j & Scoresheet v2.0.0 { **[S01,S04]**})]

All temperature inputs and calculations are strictly in **degrees Celsius ($°C$)** (`Rule 6.b`). High score wins ($\max \mathrm{FS} = 100.0\text{ pts}$):

$$
\begin{aligned}

  \mathrm{FS} = \mathrm{ES} + \mathrm{TS} + \mathrm{PS}, \quad
  \mathrm{ES} = 50 \times \frac{\text{Part I Score}}{\text{Highest Part I}}, \quad
  \mathrm{TS} = 30 \times M_{\mathrm{pen}} \times \frac{\mathrm{TG}}{\text{Highest }\mathrm{TG}}, \quad
  \mathrm{PS} = 20 \times M_{\mathrm{pen}} \times \frac{\mathrm{PE}}{\text{Highest }\mathrm{PE}}
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}

  \mathrm{TG} = \max\!\left(0,\; T_f - T_i\right)\ [°C], \qquad
  \mathrm{PE} = \max\!\left(0,\; 1 - \frac{\left|T_f - T_{\mathrm{pred}}\right|}{T_f}\right)\ \left(T \text{ in }°C\right), \qquad
  M_{\mathrm{pen}} = (0.7)^{V_c} \times (0.9)^{V_p}
\end{aligned}
$$
- **Construction Violations ($V_c$, $\times 0.7$ each to $\mathrm{TS},\mathrm{PS}$, Rule `6.h` & Box 3):** Unfixed violations at end of 3-min Setup across `2.d` (non-impound/temp  **[S02]**), `3.b.ii` (probes/thermoses/coolers/vacuum), `3.c` (9 oz cup fit), `3.d` ($30.0 cm$ cube), `3.e` (water contact/additives), `3.g` (room temp), `3.h` (Building Policy).
- **Competition Violations ($V_p$, $\times 0.9$ each to $\mathrm{TS},\mathrm{PS}$, Rule `6.g` & Box 5):** Violations of `5.II.b` (post-setup modification beyond cup insert/remove) or `5.II.d` (altering cup/water, tape/adhesives/clips on cup  **[S02]**, or swirling/stirring water  **[S02]**).
- **Official Tiebreakers (`Rule 6.j`  **[S04]**):** **1st (`TB1`): Best $\mathrm{TS}$**; **2nd (`TB2`): Best $\mathrm{ES}$**; **3rd (`TB3`): Preselected written test questions**.

| **Constr. $V_c$** | $\mathbf{V_p = 0}$ | $\mathbf{V_p = 1}$ | $\mathbf{V_p = 2}$ | **Hard Zero-Score Triggers ($\mathrm{TS}=0$ and/or $\mathrm{PS}=0$; $\mathrm{ES}$ unaffected)** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\mathbf{V_c = 0}$ | $\mathbf{1.0000}$ | $0.9000$ | $0.8100$ | • **Hazardous Material (`3.b.i/iii`, Box 1 = F):** Asbestos, mineral wool, fiberglass, or **Styrofoam / `#6 PS`** **[S02]** $\Rightarrow$ Device not tested; $\mathbf{\mathrm{TS}=0,\;\mathrm{PS}=0}$. |
| $\mathbf{V_c = 1}$ | $0.7000$ | $0.6300$ | $0.5670$ | • **Internal Energy Source (`3.f`, Box 2 = F):** Heaters, electricity, chemicals $\Rightarrow \mathbf{\mathrm{TS}=0,\;\mathrm{PS}=0}$. |

### Worked Example — Clean Run vs. Stacked Penalty Audit on a 55-Team Invitational Field `[2027 Rule 6.c–h]`

At an invitational where field highs are $\max(\text{Part I}) = 85.00\text{ pts}$ (out of $238.0$, Cornell 2027 `E1`  **[S25]**), $\max(\mathrm{TG}) = 16.0 °C$, and $\max(\mathrm{PE}) = 0.9950$, **Team Alpha** scores $78.20\text{ pts}$ on Part I, starts at $T_i = 21.4 °C$, predicts $T_{\mathrm{pred}} = 36.3 °C$, and reaches $T_f = 36.6 °C$ ($V_c = V_p = 0$). **Team Beta** achieves identical raw numbers but failed to impound a spare lid ($V_c = 1$, `2.d`  **[S02]**) and taped cling wrap to the cup ($V_p = 1$, `5.II.d`  **[S02]**). Compute both Final Scores.
**Solution.** For **Team Alpha** ($M_{\mathrm{pen}} = 1.0000$): $\mathrm{ES}_\alpha = 50(78.20/85.00) = 46.0000\text{ pts}$, $\mathrm{TG}_\alpha = 36.6 - 21.4 = 15.2 °C \implies \mathrm{TS}_\alpha = 30(15.2/16.0) = 28.5000\text{ pts}$, and $\mathrm{PE}_\alpha = 1 - 0.3/36.6 = 0.991803 \implies \mathrm{PS}_\alpha = 20(0.991803/0.9950) = 19.9357\text{ pts}$, giving $\mathrm{FS}_\alpha = 46.0000 + 28.5000 + 19.9357 = \mathbf{94.4357 \approx 94.44\text{**pts**}}$.
For **Team Beta**, $M_{\mathrm{pen},\beta} = (0.7)^1(0.9)^1 = 0.6300$ multiplies $\mathrm{TS}$ and $\mathrm{PS}$ ($\mathrm{ES}_\beta = 46.0000$ unchanged): $\mathrm{TS}_\beta = 28.5000(0.63) = 17.9550\text{ pts}$ and $\mathrm{PS}_\beta = 19.935744(0.63) = 12.5595\text{ pts}$, yielding $\mathrm{FS}_\beta = \mathbf{76.5145 \approx 76.51\text{**pts**}}$ (a loss of $\mathbf{17.92\text{**overall points**}}$!).

**✓ Verified by:** Independent Python check `SEC00_EX01_CLEAN_SCORE` & `SEC00_EX01_PENALTY_STACK` against Scoresheet v2.0.0 formulas.

### Worked Example — Tiebreaker Resolution (`TB1 = Best TS`) & The Celsius Denominator in $\mathrm{PE}$ `[2027 Rule 6.b, 6.f, 6.j]`

(a) **Team Gamma** ($\mathrm{ES}=44.00, \mathrm{TS}=29.00, \mathrm{PS}=18.50$) and **Team Delta** ($\mathrm{ES}=45.50, \mathrm{TS}=27.50, \mathrm{PS}=18.50$) tie at $\mathrm{FS} = 91.50\text{ pts}$. Who wins? (b) At $T_f = 32.0 °C$ ($\max\mathrm{PE}=1.000, M_{\mathrm{pen}}=1$), how many $\mathrm{PS}$ points does a $0.40 °C$ prediction error cost, and by what factor does a Kelvin denominator misestimate it?
**Solution.** (a) Under Rule `6.j`, **1st Tiebreaker (`TB1`) is Best $\mathrm{TS}$**, *not* Best $\mathrm{ES}$. Because $\mathrm{TS}_\gamma = 29.00 > \mathrm{TS}_\delta = 27.50$, **Team Gamma wins the tie** despite a lower written score.
(b) In Celsius (`Rule 6.b`), $\Delta\mathrm{PE} = |\Delta T_{\mathrm{err}}|/T_f = 0.40/32.0 = 0.01250$, costing $\Delta\mathrm{PS} = 20(0.01250) = \mathbf{0.250\text{**pts**}}$. Using $T_f = 305.15 K$ gives $\Delta\mathrm{PE}_K = 0.001311$, underestimating point sensitivity by $305.15/32.0 = \mathbf{9.536\times}$.

**✓ Verified by:** Independent Python check `SEC00_EX02_TIEBREAKER_AND_PE_TRAP` (`verify/checks/check_sec00.py`).

### [TRAP & DIAGNOSTIC: Top 4 Catastrophic 2027 Rules & Scoring Traps to Eliminate Before Impound]

| **Wrong move / Symptom** | **What it produces / Why it fails** | **5-second diagnostic & fix** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Styrofoam or `#6 PS` anywhere in device | Violates `3.b.i` hazardous rule (`Clarif. #6` **[S02]**); barred from Part II ($\mathrm{TS}=\mathrm{PS}=0$). | Use only cork, balsa, cardboard, cotton, wool, or foil air gaps (§`sec:14`). |
| Taping or clipping wrap to the 9 oz cup | Violates `5.II.d` (`Clarif. #5` **[S02]**) $\Rightarrow \times 0.9$ competition penalty. | Rest a loose clear BoPET disc on the rim with **zero tape/clips** (§`sec:15`). |
| Swirling cup or leaving wrap on for $T_f$ | Violates `5.II.g` (`Clarif. #1–#3` **[S02]**) and destroys top-layer thermal stratification. | Lift cup vertically without sloshing and strip off BoPET cap before $T_f$. |
| Late $T_{\mathrm{pred}}$ after Heating Time ends | Rule `5.II.f` & `6.f.iv`: late prediction gives $\mathbf{\mathrm{PS} = 0}$ ($-20\text{ pts}$). | File $T_{\mathrm{pred}}$ card at $t = 5 min$ into Heating Time ($\ge 5 min$ early!). |

| **If the Question Asks For\dots** | **Quick Sheet** | **Chapter** | **Primary Governing Equation (Algebra-Only `5.d.iv`)** | **Critical Trap Check** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Temp conversion across `K, °C, °F, °R, °De, °N, °Ré, °Rø` | **QS-01** (§`sec:01.1`) | §`sec:03` | $\frac{T_C}{100}=\frac{T_F-32}{180}=\frac{T_{\mathrm{Re}}}{80}=\frac{100-T_{\mathrm{De}}}{150}=\frac{T_N}{33}=\frac{T_{\mathrm{Ro}}-7.5}{52.5}$ | Delisle ($°\mathrm{De}$) is *inverted* ($0\,^\circ\mathrm{De}=100 °C$); intervals scale by ratio only! |
| 8 Named Scientists (`5.c.v`) or historical apparatus | **QS-14** (§`sec:01.14`) | §`sec:03` | Black ($L, c$), Carnot ($\eta_C$), Joule ($J$), Kelvin ($T$), Clausius ($S$), Maxwell ($f(v)$), Boltzmann ($k_B\ln\Omega$), Planck ($h\nu$) | Black held caloric theory; Rumford (cannon) & Joule (paddle) disproved it. |
| Linear/volume expansion, bimetallic strip, thermal stress | **QS-02** (§`sec:01.2`) | §`sec:03` | $\Delta L = \alpha L_0\Delta T$, $\Delta V_{\mathrm{over}} = (\beta_{\mathrm{liq}}-3\alpha_{\mathrm{ves}})V_0\Delta T$, $\sigma = -E\alpha\Delta T$, $R_{\mathrm{curv}} \approx \frac{t}{(\alpha_2-\alpha_1)\Delta T}$ | Water contracts from $0 °C\to4 °C$ ($\beta < 0$ below $4 °C$ **[S09]**). |
| Ice + water + steam final $T_f$ and phase masses | **QS-03** (§`sec:01.3`) | §`sec:04` | Compare $Q_{\mathrm{avail}}$ vs. $Q_{\mathrm{melt}} = m_i c_i\|T_i\| + m_i L_f$ before solving sensible balance $\sum m_k c_k(T_f-T_k)=0$ | Never assume all ice melts; check $0 °C$ and $100 °C$ enthalpy thresholds first! |
| Coffee-cup vs. bomb calorimetry ($\Delta H$ vs. $\Delta U$) | **QS-03** (§`sec:01.3`) | §`sec:04` | $q_V = \Delta U$ (isochoric bomb); $q_P = \Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_{\mathrm{gas}}RT$ (isobaric coffee cup) | Convert $\Delta n_{\mathrm{gas}}RT$ in J to kJ before adding to $\Delta U$ (kJ/mol). |
| $P$–$T$ phase diagram, vapor quality $x$, or alloy lever rule | **QS-04** (§`sec:01.4`) | §`sec:05` | $v = v_f + x(v_g-v_f)$; binary lever rule $f_L = \frac{w_0 - w_S}{w_L - w_S}$, $f_S = \frac{w_L - w_0}{w_L - w_S}$ | $\mathrm{H_2O}$ fusion slope $dP/dT < 0$ (ice I less dense than liquid; Ice III has $dP/dT > 0$). |
| Clausius–Clapeyron vapor pressure $P_{\mathrm{sat}}(T)$ | **QS-04** (§`sec:01.4`) | §`sec:05` | $\ln\!\left(\frac{P_2}{P_1}\right) = -\frac{\Delta H_{\mathrm{vap}}}{R}\!\left(\frac{1}{T_2} - \frac{1}{T_1}\right)$ | Both $T_1, T_2$ must be in K and $R = 8.31446 J/mol/K$. |
| Kinetic theory speeds ($v_{\mathrm{mp}}, v_{\mathrm{avg}}, v_{\mathrm{rms}}$) or $C_V, \gamma$ | **QS-05** (§`sec:01.5`) | §`sec:06` | $v_{\mathrm{rms}}=\sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}$, $v_{\mathrm{avg}}=\sqrt{\frac{8RT}{\pi M}}$, $v_{\mathrm{mp}}=\sqrt{\frac{2RT}{M}}$; $C_{V,m}=\frac{f}{2}R$, $\gamma=1+\frac{2}{f}$ | Molar mass $M$ must be in **kg/mol** (e.g. $\mathrm{N_2} = 0.028014 kg/mol$), not g/mol! |
| 1st Law $\Delta U, Q, W_{\mathrm{by}}$ for ideal-gas process | **QS-06** (§`sec:01.6`) | §`sec:07` | $\Delta U = nC_{V,m}\Delta T = Q - W_{\mathrm{by}}$; Isothermal $W_{\mathrm{by}}=nRT\ln\frac{V_2}{V_1}$; Adiabatic $W_{\mathrm{by}}=\frac{P_1V_1-P_2V_2}{\gamma-1}$ | $\Delta U = nC_{V,m}\Delta T$ holds for *every* ideal-gas process (even isobaric!). |
| Entropy $\Delta S$, Gibbs $\Delta G$, or exergy destruction **[STATE/NAT]** | **QS-07** (§`sec:01.7`) | §`sec:08` | $\Delta S = mc\ln\frac{T_2}{T_1} + \frac{mL}{T_{\mathrm{tr}}}$; $\Delta S_{\mathrm{IG}} = nC_{V,m}\ln\frac{T_2}{T_1} + nR\ln\frac{V_2}{V_1}$; $X_{\mathrm{dest}} = T_0\Delta S_{\mathrm{univ}}$ | Free expansion of ideal gas: $Q=0, W=0, \Delta T=0$, but $\Delta S_{\mathrm{sys}} = nR\ln(V_2/V_1) > 0$! |
| Engine $\eta$, Refrigerator/HP COP, or named cycle | **QS-08** (§`sec:01.8`) | §`sec:09` | $\eta = \frac{W_{\mathrm{net}}}{Q_{\mathrm{in}}} \le 1-\frac{T_C}{T_H}$; $\mathrm{COP}_R = \frac{Q_C}{W_{\mathrm{in}}}$; $\mathrm{COP}_{\mathrm{HP}} = \mathrm{COP}_R + 1$; $\eta_{\mathrm{Otto}} = 1 - r^{1-\gamma}$ | $Q_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the sum of *positive heat inflows only*, never net $Q$! |
| Composite wall, pipe, or sphere conduction | **QS-09** (§`sec:01.9`) | §`sec:10` | $\dot{Q} = \frac{\Delta T}{\sum R_{\mathrm{th}}}$; $R_{\mathrm{slab}}=\frac{L}{kA}$, $R_{\mathrm{cyl}}=\frac{\ln(r_o/r_i)}{2\pi k l}$, $R_{\mathrm{sph}}=\frac{r_o-r_i}{4\pi k r_i r_o}$, $r_{\mathrm{crit}}=\frac{k}{h}$ | Series layers add resistances $R_{\mathrm{th}}$, parallel paths add conductances $1/R_{\mathrm{th}}$. |
| Convection, dead-air gap, or evaporative loss | **QS-10** (§`sec:01.10`) | §`sec:11` | $\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{conv}} = hA(T_s-T_\infty)$, $\mathrm{Ra}_L = \frac{g\beta\Delta T L^3}{\nu\alpha}$, $\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{evap}} = \dot{m}_{\mathrm{evap}}L_v$ | Enclosed horizontal air gaps convect once $\mathrm{Ra}_\delta > 1708$ ($\delta \gtrsim 12 mm$). |
| Blackbody radiation, Wien peak, or $N$ shields **[STATE/NAT]** | **QS-11** (§`sec:01.11`) | §`sec:12` | $\dot{Q}_{12} = \frac{\sigma(T_1^4-T_2^4)}{\frac{1-\varepsilon_1}{\varepsilon_1 A_1}+\frac{1}{A_1 F_{12}}+\frac{1-\varepsilon_2}{\varepsilon_2 A_2}}$; $N$ equal shields: $\dot{Q}_N = \frac{\dot{Q}_0}{N+1}$ | Always convert $T$ to **Kelvin** before raising to the 4th power ($T^4$)! |
| 2027 Collector heating curve & $T_{\mathrm{pred}}$ prediction | **QS-12, 13** (§`sec:01.13`) | §`sec:13`, §`sec:16` | $T(t) = T_{\mathrm{ss}} - (T_{\mathrm{ss}} - T_i)e^{-t/\tau}$, $T_{\mathrm{ss}} = T_{\mathrm{amb}} + \dot{Q}_{\mathrm{abs}}R_{\mathrm{th}}$, $\tau = R_{\mathrm{th}}C_{\mathrm{eff}}$ | Apply top-layer stratification factor $\kappa_{\mathrm{strat}} \ge 1.25$ for unstirred ES reading **[S02]**. |

## 50-Minute Hybrid Event Choreography & Two-Partner Protocol

> **[Vector Figure: 50-minute hybrid event partner choreography showing how Partner B completes all device setup, water insertion, $T_{\mathrm{pred}}$ card filing, and unstirred cup extraction in $\le 9 min$ total while contributing $> 40 min$ to the written exam alongside Partner A. | Label: `fig:00:timeline`]**
> - **Diagram Annotations & Key Elements:** Partner B / (Device + / Exam) • **Setup** / (3m) • Cup • Calc & File / $T_{\mathrm{pred}}$ Card • Written Exam / (`5.c.i,v`) • $T_f$ • **Full-Time Written Exam Co-Solver** (`5.c.iii` Transfer, `5.c.vi` Radiation, Lab/Data FRQs) — 30+ min • Pass 3 / Audit • Partner A / (Written / Lead) • **Pass 1 (0–25 min):** Sweep all Tier 1–2 Points (`5.c.i–v, vii`) + 20s $T_{\mathrm{pred}}$ Check at $t=7 min$ • **Pass 2 (25–45 min):** Deep Multi-Part Derivations (`5.c.ii, iv, vii` & `TB3` Qs) • Units & / Sig Figs

### [FORMULA & DECISION CARD: Partner Role & Detached-Page Split (`Rule 2.b–c`)]
- **Unbind & Spread Key Modules at $t=0 min$ (`Rule 2.c`):** Because pages *may be separated or removed from containers during any part of the event*, immediately pull out **Tab 6 (§`sec:16` Nomograms)** and **`QS-13`** for Partner B's device station while Partner A keeps the main binder and **12-Page QuickRef Booklet** at the exam desk.
- **Dual Class III Calculator Deployment (`Rule 2.b`):**
- **Calculator 1 (Partner A):** Dedicated to Part I multi-step calorimetry, gas/cycle tables, and steam-table interpolation.
- **Calculator 2 (Partner B):** Pre-loaded with the 2027 Collector $T_{\mathrm{pred}}(h_{\mathrm{bulb}}, t_{\mathrm{heat}}, P_{\mathrm{bulb}}, T_i, T_{\mathrm{amb}})$ solver; switches to Part I calculations at $t = 8 min$.
- **Two-Eye Prediction Verification ($t = 7 min$):** Before Partner B hands the $T_{\mathrm{pred}}$ notecard to the ES, Partner A spends $20 s$ verifying that (i) $T_{\mathrm{pred}} > T_i$, (ii) $T_{\mathrm{pred}}$ is in $°C$ to $0.1 °C$ (`5.II.f`, `6.b`), and (iii) the lookup row matches the ES-announced $(h_{\mathrm{bulb}}, t_{\mathrm{heat}}, P_{\mathrm{bulb}})$.

### [FORMULA & DECISION CARD: 3-Pass Written Exam Triage (Cornell 2027 Baseline { **[S25]**})]

**Empirical Proof (§`sec:22`):** On the 2026–2027 Cornell Invitational (`E1`, $n=55$ teams, $238.0\text{ raw pts}$), the winning raw score was $85.00/238.0$ ($35.7\% \to \mathrm{ES}=50.0$), while **Tier 1 ($25\text{ pts}$) + Tier 2 ($65\text{ pts}$) items alone totaled $90.0\text{ pts}$**. Never stall on a 15-minute derivation while leaving fast points blank!
- **Pass 1 (Minutes 0–25 — High-Velocity Sweep):**
- Partner A sweeps all Tier 1–2 questions in `5.c.ii` (calorimetry/phase diagrams), `5.c.iv` (processes/cycles), and `5.c.vii` ($\Delta S/\Delta H$).
- Partner B (from min 8–25) sweeps all Tier 1–2 questions in `5.c.i` (scales/units), `5.c.v` (8 scientists), `5.c.iii` (conduction/convection), and `5.c.vi` (Stefan–Boltzmann/Wien).
- **Pass 2 (Minutes 25–45 — Tier 3 & `TB3` Separators):** Attack multi-part derivations and designated **Tiebreaker #3 (`6.j`)** questions using §`sec:19` templates.
- **Pass 3 (Minutes 45–50 — Zero-Defect Unit & Sig-Fig Audit):** Verify every answer carries **metric units and correct significant figures** (`Rule 5.I.b`  **[S06]**).

### [TRAP & DIAGNOSTIC: Six Exact Temperature-Scale Intersections & Interval vs. Point-Temperature Trap { **[S07,S13]**}]

**Exact Crossovers:**
(**1**) $^\circ\mathrm{C} = {^\circ\mathrm{F}}$ at $\mathbf{-40^\circ}$ ($233.15 K$);
(**2**) $\mathrm{K} = {^\circ\mathrm{F}}$ at $\mathbf{+574.5875}$ ($301.4375 °C$);
(**3**) $^\circ\mathrm{C} = {^\circ\mathrm{De}}$ at $\mathbf{+60^\circ}$ ($333.15 K$);
(**4**) $^\circ\mathrm{F} = {^\circ\mathrm{De}}$ at $\mathbf{+96.3636^\circ}$ ($1060/11^\circ$, where $T_C = 1180/33 = 35.7576 °C$);
(**5**) $^\circ\mathrm{C} = {^\circ}\text{Rø}$ at $\mathbf{+15.7895^\circ}$ ($+300/19^\circ$, $288.9395 K$);
(**6**) $^\circ\mathrm{C} = {^\circ}\text{Ré} = {^\circ\mathrm{N}}$ at $\mathbf{0^\circ}$ ($273.15 K$).
**Interval Trap:** A temperature *difference* converts without the additive offset: $\Delta T[\mathrm{K}] = \Delta T[^\circ\mathrm{C}] = \tfrac{5}{9}\Delta T[^\circ\mathrm{F}] = \tfrac{5}{9}\Delta T[^\circ\mathrm{R}]$. Therefore $c_w = 4184 J/kg/K \equiv 4184 J/kg/°C$ (never add $273.15$ to a denominator $\text{K}^{-1}$!).

### Worked Example — Glass Flask Overflow & Pendulum Drift `[T2 $\cdot$ 60 s]`

A Pyrex flask ($V_0 = 500.0 mL$, $\alpha_g = 3.2×10^{-6} /K$) filled to the brim with mercury ($\beta_{\mathrm{Hg}} = 181×10^{-6} /K$) is heated from $20.0 °C$ to $80.0 °C$ ($\Delta T = 60.0 K$). Find the mercury overflow $\Delta V_{\mathrm{over}}$.
**Sol.:** $\beta_{\mathrm{app}} = \beta_{\mathrm{Hg}} - 3\alpha_g = (181 - 9.6)\times 10^{-6} = 171.4×10^{-6} /K$.
$\Delta V_{\mathrm{over}} = \beta_{\mathrm{app}} V_0 \Delta T = (171.4×10^{-6})(500.0 mL)(60.0) = 5.14 mL$.

**✓ Verified by:** Exact $V_{\mathrm{Hg}} - V_{\mathrm{flask}} = 500(1.01086 - 1.000576) = 5.142 mL$.

### [TRAP & DIAGNOSTIC: Four Classic Thermal-Expansion Traps { **[S13,S35]**}]

**1. Hole / Cavity Trap:** A hole or cavity in a uniform solid expands *outward* at the exact same rate ($\alpha$ or $3\alpha$) as a solid plug of the same material.\\
**2. Water $0\text{--}4\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ Contraction:** Water *contracts* ($\beta < 0$) when warmed from $0 °C$ ($\rho = 999.84 kg/m^3$) to $3.984 °C$ ($\rho_{\max} = 999.97 kg/m^3$), then expands for $T > 4 °C$.\\
**3. Bimetallic Bend Direction:** When heated ($\Delta T > 0$), a bimetallic strip bends *toward* the lower-$\alpha$ metal (higher-$\alpha$ metal on the outside convex arc); when cooled ($\Delta T < 0$), it bends toward the higher-$\alpha$ metal.\\
**4. Ruler Scale Trap:** A metal ruler heated above its calibration temp $T_0$ expands, so its tick marks spread apart and it *under-reads* true length: $L_{\mathrm{true}} = L_{\mathrm{read}}[1 + \alpha_{\mathrm{ruler}}(T - T_0)]$.

### [FORMULA & DECISION CARD: Deterministic 5-Zone Ice ($T_{\mathrm{ice}} \le 0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$) + Liquid Water ($0\le T_w \le 100\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$) + Steam ($T_s \ge 100\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$) Algorithm { **[S09,S13]**}]

**Reference Benchmarks ($1 atm$):** $c_{\mathrm{ice}} = 2093 J/kg/K$, $c_w = 4184 J/kg/K$, $c_{\mathrm{steam},P} = 2080 J/kg/K$, $L_f = 333.4 kJ/kg$ (OpenStax $334 kJ/kg$), $L_v = 2256.4 kJ/kg$.\\
**Step 1 — Compute Energy Benchmarks Relative to $0 °C$ Liquid Water ($\Delta H_{\mathrm{ref}} = 0$ at $0 °C$ liquid):**
- Heat needed to warm subcooled ice to $0 °C$: $Q_1 = m_{\mathrm{ice}} c_{\mathrm{ice}}(0 - T_{\mathrm{ice}})$. \quad Heat needed to melt all ice at $0 °C$: $Q_2 = m_{\mathrm{ice}} L_f$.
- Heat needed to warm all melted ice + initial water to $100 °C$: $Q_3 = m_{\mathrm{ice}} c_w(100) + m_w c_w(100 - T_w)$.
- Heat released if warm water cools to $0 °C$: $Q_{w\to 0} = m_w c_w(T_w - 0)$. \quad Heat released if steam cools to $100 °C$ and condenses: $Q_{s\to 100,\ell} = m_s c_s(T_s - 100) + m_s L_v$.
- Total heat released if steam cools all the way to $0 °C$ liquid water: $Q_{s\to 0,\ell} = Q_{s\to 100,\ell} + m_s c_w(100)$. \quad Let $Q_{\mathrm{avail},0} = Q_{w\to 0} + Q_{s\to 0,\ell}$.

**Step 2 — Locate Unique Equilibrium Zone:**{

| **Condition** | **Final Phase State** | **Exact Algebraic Equation for Final Temperature $T_f$ or Phase Fraction** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Zone 1:** $Q_{\mathrm{avail},0} < Q_1$ | **100% Solid Ice** ($T_f < 0 °C$) | $T_f = -\dfrac{Q_1 - Q_{\mathrm{avail},0}}{(m_{\mathrm{ice}} + m_w + m_s)c_{\mathrm{ice}}}\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ (all water/steam freezes and subcools) |
| **Zone 2:** $Q_1 \le Q_{\mathrm{avail},0} \le Q_1 + Q_2$ | **Ice–Water Slush at $T_f = 0.0 °C$** | Mass of ice melted: $m_{\mathrm{melted}} = \dfrac{Q_{\mathrm{avail},0} - Q_1}{L_f}$; remaining ice $= m_{\mathrm{ice}} - m_{\mathrm{melted}}$ |
| **Zone 3:** $Q_1+Q_2 < Q_{\mathrm{avail},0} < Q_1+Q_2+(m_{\mathrm{ice}}+m_w+m_s)c_w(100)$ | **100% Liquid Water** ($0 °C < T_f < 100 °C$) | $T_f = \dfrac{Q_{\mathrm{avail},0} - (Q_1 + Q_2)}{(m_{\mathrm{ice}} + m_w + m_s)c_w}\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ |
| **Zone 4:** $0 \le Q_{s\to 100,\ell} - (Q_1+Q_2+Q_3) \le (m_{\mathrm{ice}}+m_w)L_v$ | **Water–Steam Mix at $T_f = 100.0 °C$** | Mass of steam condensed: $m_{\mathrm{cond}} = \dfrac{Q_1 + Q_2 + Q_3 - m_s c_s(T_s-100)}{L_v}$ |
| **Zone 5:** $m_s c_s(T_s - 100) > Q_1 + Q_2 + Q_3 + (m_{\mathrm{ice}}+m_w)L_v$ | **100% Superheated Steam** ($T_f > 100 °C$) | $T_f = 100 + \dfrac{m_s c_s(T_s-100) - [Q_1+Q_2+Q_3+(m_{\mathrm{ice}}+m_w)L_v]}{(m_{\mathrm{ice}}+m_w+m_s)c_s}\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ |

### Worked Example — Three-Phase Ice + Warm Water + Steam Calorimeter Check `[T2 $\cdot$ 75 s]`

Mix $m_{\mathrm{ice}} = 50.0 g$ ice at $-20.0 °C$, $m_w = 200.0 g$ liquid water at $30.0 °C$, and $m_s = 10.0 g$ steam at $100.0 °C$ at $1 atm$ ($c_{\mathrm{ice}}=2.093 J/g/K, c_w=4.184 J/g/K, L_f=333.4 J/g, L_v=2256.4 J/g$). Find $T_f$.
**Sol.:** $Q_1 = 50(2.093)(20) = 2093 J$; $Q_2 = 50(333.4) = 16670 J$, so $Q_1+Q_2 = 18763 J$. Available heat to $0 °C$ liquid: $Q_{w\to 0} = 200(4.184)(30) = 25104 J$; $Q_{s\to 0,\ell} = 10(2256.4) + 10(4.184)(100) = 26748 J$, so $Q_{\mathrm{avail},0} = 51852 J > 18763 J$ (Zone 3: 100% liquid). Total mass $M = 260.0 g$:
$T_f = (51852 - 18763)/[260.0 \times 4.184] = 33089 J/(1087.84 J/K) = 30.42 °C$.

**✓ Verified by:** Direct energy balance at $30.417\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$: $Q_{\mathrm{gain,ice}} = 2093+16670+50(4.184)(30.417) = 25126 J$; $Q_{\mathrm{loss},w+s} = 25126 J$.

### Worked Example — Binary Eutectic Lever Rule (`2027 Cornell E1` Style) `[T2 $\cdot$ 60 s]`

In the $\mathrm{Al\text{--}Cu}$ system, the eutectic reaction $L \to \alpha + \theta$ occurs at $T_E = 548 °C$ with eutectic composition $w_E = 33.2 wt\%\ Cu$ and terminal solid solubility $w_\alpha = 5.65 wt\%\ Cu$, $w_\theta = 52.5 wt\%\ Cu$. For an alloy of overall composition $w_0 = 20.0 wt\%\ Cu$ cooled just below $548 °C$, find (a) the total mass fraction of $\alpha$ phase and (b) the mass fraction of the *eutectic microconstituent*.
**Sol.:** (a) Across the full $\alpha$–$\theta$ tie-line $[5.65, 52.5]$:
$f_{\alpha,\mathrm{tot}} = \dfrac{w_\theta - w_0}{w_\theta - w_\alpha} = \dfrac{52.5 - 20.0}{52.5 - 5.65} = \dfrac{32.5}{46.85} = 0.6937$ ($69.4\%$), $f_\theta = 0.3063$.
(b) Just above $T_E$, liquid has $w_L = w_E = 33.2\%$, so primary (proeutectic) $\alpha$ is $f_{\alpha,\mathrm{prim}} = \frac{33.2 - 20.0}{33.2 - 5.65} = 0.4791$ and the eutectic microconstituent fraction is $f_{\mathrm{eut}} = \frac{20.0 - 5.65}{33.2 - 5.65} = \frac{14.35}{27.55} = 0.5209$ ($52.1\%$).

**✓ Verified by:** Copper mass balance: $0.47913(5.65) + 0.52087(33.2) = 20.000\,\mathrm{wt\%}$.

### [TRAP & DIAGNOSTIC: Three High-Frequency Gas & Kinetic-Theory Traps { **[S10,S13]**}]

**1. Molar Mass in $g/mol$ Trap:** In $v_{\mathrm{rms}} = \sqrt{3RT/M}$, using $M = 28$ instead of $M = 0.028013 kg/mol$ makes $v_{\mathrm{rms}}$ too small by $\sqrt{1000} = 31.62\times$!\\
**2. Mixture Heat-Capacity Ratio Trap:** For a gas mixture ($n_1, n_2$), compute $C_{V,\mathrm{mix}} = \sum x_i C_{V,i}$ and $C_{P,\mathrm{mix}} = \sum x_i C_{P,i}$ *first*, then take $\gamma_{\mathrm{mix}} = C_{P,\mathrm{mix}}/C_{V,\mathrm{mix}}$. Never take the mole-fraction average of $\gamma_i$!\\
**3. Vibrational Freeze-Out ($\mathrm{H_2}$ Pyramid):** For diatomic $\mathrm{H_2}$: $T < 60 K \Rightarrow f=3$ ($\gamma = 5/3$); $250 K < T < 700 K \Rightarrow f=5$ ($\gamma = 7/5$); $T > 3000 K \Rightarrow f=7$ ($\gamma = 9/7$). Each classical vibrational mode adds $2$ DOF ($K_{\mathrm{vib}} + U_{\mathrm{vib}}$), so $C_{\mathrm{vib},m} = R$ per active vibrational mode.

### [ONE-PAGE QUICK SHEET: QS-06 — First Law Sign Conventions, 7-Process Master Table & $P$–$V$/$T$–$S$ Atlas]

### [FORMULA & DECISION CARD: Locked Physics vs. Chemistry First-Law Sign Translation { **[S13,S16]**}]

**Physics Convention (Locked across Binder):** $\mathbf{\Delta U = Q - W_{\mathrm{by}}}$, where $Q > 0$ enters system and $W_{\mathrm{by}} = \int_{V_1}^{V_2} P\,dV > 0$ is expansion work **by** system.\\
**Chemistry / IUPAC Convention:** $\mathbf{\Delta U = q + w_{\mathrm{on}}}$, where $w_{\mathrm{on}} = -W_{\mathrm{by}} = -\int_{V_1}^{V_2} P_{\mathrm{ext}}\,dV > 0$ is compression work **on** system.\\
**Ideal Gas Identities (Always True for Any Process if $C_V, C_P$ are Constant):** $\Delta U = n C_{V,m}\Delta T = \dfrac{P_2 V_2 - P_1 V_1}{\gamma - 1}$ and $\Delta H = n C_{P,m}\Delta T = \gamma\,\Delta U$.

| **Process ($PV^n=\mathrm{C}$)** | **Constraint** | **State Relation (**[IDEAL-GAS]**)** | **$\Delta U$** | **Work $W_{\mathrm{by}}$** | **Heat Added $Q$** | **Entropy $\Delta S_{\mathrm{sys}}$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Isochoric** ($n\to\infty$) | $V = \mathrm{const}$ | $P_1/T_1 = P_2/T_2$ | $n C_{V,m}\Delta T$ | $0$ | $n C_{V,m}\Delta T = \Delta U$ | $n C_{V,m}\ln(T_2/T_1)$ |
| **Isobaric** ($n=0$) | $P = \mathrm{const}$ | $V_1/T_1 = V_2/T_2$ | $n C_{V,m}\Delta T$ | $P(V_2 - V_1) = nR\Delta T$ | $n C_{P,m}\Delta T = \Delta H$ | $n C_{P,m}\ln(T_2/T_1)$ |
| **Isothermal** ($n=1$) | $T = \mathrm{const}$ | $P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2$ | $0$ (**[IDEAL-GAS]**) | $nRT\ln(V_2/V_1)$ | $W_{\mathrm{by}} = nRT\ln(V_2/V_1)$ | $nR\ln(V_2/V_1)$ |
| **Adiabatic Rev.** ($n=\gamma$) | $Q=0, S=\mathrm{C}$ | $PV^\gamma=\mathrm{C}, TV^{\gamma-1}=\mathrm{C}$ | $n C_{V,m}\Delta T$ | $-\Delta U = \dfrac{P_1V_1 - P_2V_2}{\gamma - 1}$ | $0$ | $0$ |
| **Polytropic** ($n\ne 1$) | $PV^n = \mathrm{const}$ | $TV^{n-1}=\mathrm{C}, T^n P^{1-n}=\mathrm{C}$ | $n C_{V,m}\Delta T$ | $\dfrac{P_1V_1 - P_2V_2}{n - 1}$ | $n C_n \Delta T$, $C_n = C_{V,m}\dfrac{n-\gamma}{n-1}$ | $n C_n \ln(T_2/T_1)$ |
| **Joule Free Exp.** | $Q=0, W=0$ | Vacuum expansion $V_1 \to V_2$ | $0$ ($T_2=T_1$ **[IDEAL-GAS]**) | $0$ ($P_{\mathrm{ext}}=0$) | $0$ | $+nR\ln(V_2/V_1) > 0$ |
| **J–T Throttling** | $H = \mathrm{const}$ | Steady porous plug/valve | $0$ (**[IDEAL-GAS]**); $\ne 0$ real | Flow $P_2V_2 - P_1V_1$ | $0$ | $+nR\ln(P_1/P_2)$ |

### [TRAP & DIAGNOSTIC: Slope Ratio & Irreversible Step-Pressure Trap]

**1. Slope Ratio on $P$–$V$ vs. $T$–$S$:**
On $P$–$V$, the adiabat is steeper than the isotherm by $\gamma$: $(\partial P/\partial V)_S = -\gamma P/V = \gamma(\partial P/\partial V)_T$.
On $T$–$S$, the isochore is steeper than the isobar by $\gamma$: $(\partial T/\partial S)_V = T/(nC_{V,m}) = \gamma(\partial T/\partial S)_P$.\\
**2. Irreversible Constant-$P_{\mathrm{ext}}$ Step:**
If an ideal gas expands against a *sudden constant external pressure* $P_{\mathrm{ext}} = P_2$, work is the rectangle $W_{\mathrm{by}} = P_2(V_2 - V_1)$, NOT $nRT\ln(V_2/V_1)$ and NOT $(P_1V_1-P_2V_2)/(\gamma-1)$! For an adiabatic step against $P_2$, solve $nC_{V,m}(T_2-T_1) = -P_2(V_2-V_1) = -nR P_2(T_2/P_2 - T_1/P_1)$.

> **[SCOPE: TIER-DEPENDENT | 2027 Rule 5.c.iv (2nd Law All Levels) & 5.c.vi–vii (Third Law, Entropy & Enthalpy State/National Tier; Tested on 100% of Corpus Exams  **[S25]**)]**

| $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S = \Delta G^\circ + RT\ln Q_r;\quad \Delta G^\circ = -RT\ln K_{\mathrm{eq}}$ | Van't Hoff: $\ln\!\left(\dfrac{K_2}{K_1}\right) = -\dfrac{\Delta H^\circ}{R}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{T_2} - \dfrac{1}{T_1}\right)$; Kirchhoff: $\Delta H(T_2) = \Delta H(T_1) + \Delta C_P \Delta T$ | Fixed $T, P$ | Chemical equilibrium, spontaneity ($\Delta G < 0$) |
| $W_{\mathrm{rev,max}} = -\Delta(U - T_0 S + P_0 V);\quad X_{\mathrm{dest}} = T_0 S_{\mathrm{gen}} \ge 0$ | Dead state $(T_0, P_0)$; stream flow exergy $\psi = (h - h_0) - T_0(s - s_0)$ | Exergy / 2nd Law | Gouy–Stodola lost work & 2nd-law efficiency $\eta_{\mathrm{II}}$ |

| **Potential** | **Definition** | **Natural Differential** | **Maxwell Relation** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Internal $U(S,V)$ | $U$ | $dU = T\,dS - P\,dV$ | $(\partial T/\partial V)_S = -(\partial P/\partial S)_V$ |
| Enthalpy $H(S,P)$ | $U + PV$ | $dH = T\,dS + V\,dP$ | $(\partial T/\partial P)_S = +(\partial V/\partial S)_P$ |
| Helmholtz $F(T,V)$ | $U - TS$ | $dF = -S\,dT - P\,dV$ | $(\partial S/\partial V)_T = +(\partial P/\partial T)_V$ |
| Gibbs $G(T,P)$ | $H - TS$ | $dG = -S\,dT + V\,dP$ | $(\partial S/\partial P)_T = -(\partial V/\partial T)_P$ |

### [TIER: STATE & NATIONALS (Rule 5.c.vi–vii): Third Law & Low-$T$ Heat Capacities { **[S01,S15]**}]

**Nernst–Planck Statement:** As $T \to 0\,K$, the entropy of any perfect crystal approaches zero ($S \to 0$) and $\Delta S \to 0$ for any isothermal process. Consequently, $T = 0 K$ is unattainable in a finite number of steps, and $C_V, C_P, \alpha_L, \beta \to 0$ as $T \to 0\,K$ ($C_{\mathrm{Debye}} = \tfrac{12\pi^4}{5}nR(T/\Theta_D)^3 \propto T^3$; metals add electronic $\gamma_e T$).

### Worked Example — Reversible Engine vs. Irreversible Heat Transfer between Finite Bodies `[T3 $\cdot$ 75 s]`

Two identical copper blocks ($C = m c = 1000 J/K$ each) start at $T_{1,i} = 400 K$ and $T_{2,i} = 200 K$. Compare (a) direct contact ($W = 0$) with (b) running a reversible Carnot engine between them until they reach a common final temperature.
**Sol.:** (a) Direct contact ($\sum Q = 0$): $T_f = \tfrac{1}{2}(400 + 200) = 300.0 K$, and $\Delta S_{\mathrm{univ}} = C\ln(300/400) + C\ln(300/200) = 1000\ln(90000/80000) = 1000\ln(9/8) = +117.78 J/K$.
(b) Reversible engine ($\Delta S_{\mathrm{univ}} = 0$): $C\ln(T_f'/T_{1,i}) + C\ln(T_f'/T_{2,i}) = 0 \implies T_f' = \sqrt{T_{1,i}T_{2,i}} = \sqrt{400\times 200} = 282.84 K$, producing maximum work $W_{\max} = C(T_{1,i} + T_{2,i} - 2T_f') = 1000(600 - 565.685) = 34.31 kJ$.

**✓ Verified by:** Gouy–Stodola check at $T_f'=282.84\,\text{K}$: $W_{\max} > 0$ because arithmetic mean $300\,\text{K} >$ geometric mean $282.84\,\text{K}$.

### [TRAP & DIAGNOSTIC: Clockwise vs. Counterclockwise Loop & Polygon Cycle $Q_H$ Separation Trap]

**1. Cycle Orientation:** On both $P$–$V$ and $T$–$S$ planes, a **clockwise** loop is a heat engine ($W_{\mathrm{net}} = \text{enclosed area} > 0$), while a **counterclockwise** loop is a refrigerator/heat pump ($W_{\mathrm{net}} < 0$, work input required).
**2. Polygon $P$–$V$ Cycle Trap:** For a rectangular or triangular cycle on $P$–$V$, compute $Q_{\mathrm{leg}} = \Delta U_{\mathrm{leg}} + W_{\mathrm{by,leg}}$ on *every individual leg* separately; $Q_H$ is the sum of ONLY the positive-$Q$ legs (never include a heat-rejection leg $Q_{\mathrm{leg}} < 0$ inside $Q_H$!).

### Worked Example — Fastener Thermal-Bridge Short-Circuit `[T2 $\cdot$ 60 s]`

An insulation panel ($A_{\mathrm{ins}} = 0.100 m^2$, $L = 20.0 mm$, $k_{\mathrm{ins}} = 0.040 W/m/K$) is pierced by four aluminum bolts (total area $A_{\mathrm{bolt}} = 1.00×10^{-4} m^2 = 1.00 cm^2$, $L = 20.0 mm$, $k_{\mathrm{Al}} = 237 W/m/K$). Find the percentage increase in conductive heat loss caused by the bolts.
**Sol.:** Parallel conductances $G = kA/L$:
$G_{\mathrm{ins}} = (0.040)(0.0999)/0.020 = 0.200 W/K$ ($R_{\mathrm{ins}} = 5.00 K/W$).
$G_{\mathrm{bolt}} = (237)(1.00×10^{-4})/0.020 = 1.185 W/K$ ($R_{\mathrm{bolt}} = 0.844 K/W$).
$G_{\mathrm{tot}} = 0.200 + 1.185 = 1.385 W/K$ ($R_{\mathrm{tot}} = 0.722 K/W$).
Even though the bolts occupy only $0.10\%$ of the area, they carry $85.6\%$ of the heat flow and increase total heat loss by $\mathbf{6.93\times}$ ($+593\%$)!

**✓ Verified by:** $G_{\mathrm{tot}}/G_{\mathrm{ins,0}} = 1.3848 / 0.2000 = 6.924\times$.

### [2027 HEAT-COLLECTOR DEVICE & LAB: 9 oz Cup Critical Radius Verification { **[S01,S12]**}]

For the 9 oz cup ($r_i \approx 35 mm$) in air ($h_{\mathrm{ext}} \approx 10 W/m^2/K$) with cork/wool insulation ($k \approx 0.040 W/m/K$), $r_{\mathrm{crit}} = k/h_{\mathrm{ext}} = 4.0 mm$. Because $r_i = 35 mm \gg r_{\mathrm{crit}} = 4.0 mm$, wrapping insulation around the cup **always reduces heat loss**.

### [2027 HEAT-COLLECTOR DEVICE & LAB: Evaporation Suppression Worth $+3.5\text{ to }+6.0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ { **[S02,S12]**}]

Because $L_v(35 °C) = 2418 kJ/kg$, evaporating just $0.60 g$ of water during a 10-minute run removes $1451 J$, dropping a $100 mL$ cup by $\mathbf{3.47 °C}$! Resting an unattached clear BoPET film disk over the cup mouth (`Clarification #5`, removed before final measurement) eliminates $\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{evap}}$ while transmitting $90\%$ of near-IR lamp radiation.

### [2027 HEAT-COLLECTOR DEVICE & LAB: Top-Layer Thermal Stratification Physics { **[S02,S12,S19]**}]

**Why the 9 oz Cup Stratifies Under a Top-Down Heat Lamp:**
- **Optical Surface Heating:** Near-IR water absorption ($\lambda > 1.2 µm$, $\mu_a \approx 1.0–114 /cm$) deposits $\approx 68\%$ of absorbed lamp power in the **top $10 mm$** of the $38 mm$ water column  **[S19]**.
- **Hydrostatic Buoyancy Lock:** Warm water at the top ($T_{\mathrm{top}} > T_{\mathrm{bot}} > 4 °C$) has *lower* density ($\partial\rho/\partial z > 0$ downward), suppressing Rayleigh–B\'enard convection! Downward heat transfer occurs only by slow molecular conduction ($\alpha_w = 0.145 mm^2/s \implies \delta_{\mathrm{th}}(600 s) = 2\sqrt{\alpha_w t} = 18.7 mm < 38 mm$).
- **Clarifications #1–#4 Advantage:** Neither teams nor the ES may stir or swirl the water, and the ES measures the **top water layer near the cup axis**, yielding $\mathrm{TG}_{\mathrm{top}} \approx (1.25\text{--}1.40)\,\mathrm{TG}_{\mathrm{bulk}}$ if the cup is removed smoothly without tilting!

### Worked Example — Radiation Shield Flux Reduction `[T3 $\cdot$ 60 s]`

Two parallel plates ($\varepsilon = 0.80$) at $T_1 = 400 K$ and $T_2 = 300 K$ have one thin polished Al foil shield ($\varepsilon_s = 0.040$ both sides) placed between them. Find $T_s$ and the percentage reduction in radiative flux.
**Sol.:** By symmetry, $T_s^4 = \tfrac{1}{2}(T_1^4 + T_2^4) = 1.685×10^{10}\,K^4 \implies T_s = 360.3 K$.
Without shield: $R_0'' = \tfrac{2}{0.80} - 1 = 1.50$. With shield: $R_1'' = 1.50 + (\tfrac{2}{0.040} - 1) = 50.5$. Thus $q_1''/q_0'' = 1.50/50.5 = 0.02970$, a $\mathbf{97.03\%}$ reduction ($33.7\times$ lower loss)!

**✓ Verified by:** $q_0'' = 661.5 W/m^2$; $q_1'' = 19.65 W/m^2$.

### Worked Example — Three-Point Extraction of $T_{\mathrm{ss}}$ and $\tau$ `[T3 $\cdot$ 60 s]`

In a practice lamp run, water temp is $T_1 = 22.0 °C$ at $t_1 = 0$, $T_2 = 32.0 °C$ at $t_2 = 5.0 min$, and $T_3 = 39.5 °C$ at $t_3 = 10.0 min$. Predict $T(15.0 min)$.
**Sol.:** Equal intervals $\Delta t = 5.0 min$: step gains are $\Delta_1 = 10.0 °C$ and $\Delta_2 = 7.5 °C$, so $e^{-\Delta t/\tau} = \Delta_2/\Delta_1 = 0.750$.
The third 5-min gain is $\Delta_3 = 7.5(0.750) = 5.625 °C \implies T(15.0 min) = 39.5 + 5.625 = \mathbf{45.1 °C}$ ($T_{\mathrm{ss}} = 62.0 °C$, $\tau = 17.38 min$).

**✓ Verified by:** $62.0 - 40.0(0.750)^3 = 45.125 °C$.

### [FORMULA & DECISION CARD: 3-Minute Setup Prediction Model & Official Scoring Formulas (**[2027-RULE]** 6.a–j) { **[S01,S04]**}]

**1. Day-Of Final Water Temperature Prediction Equation (in $^\circ\mathrm{C}$, rounded to $0.1 °C$):**

$$
T_{\mathrm{pred}}(h, t_{\mathrm{heat}}, P_{\mathrm{lamp}}, T_i, T_{\mathrm{room}}) = T_i + s_{\mathrm{strat}}\!\left[\frac{P_{\mathrm{abs}}(h, P_{\mathrm{lamp}})}{G_{\mathrm{loss}}} - (T_i - T_{\mathrm{room}})\right]\!\big(1 - e^{-t_{\mathrm{heat}}/\tau}\big) - \Delta T_{\mathrm{cool}}(t_{\mathrm{wait}}),\quad
  P_{\mathrm{abs}}(h) = P_{\mathrm{abs}}(h_{\mathrm{ref}})\!\left(\frac{P_{\mathrm{lamp}}}{P_{\mathrm{ref}}}\right)\!\left(\frac{h_{\mathrm{ref}} - z_{\mathrm{eff}}}{h - z_{\mathrm{eff}}}\right)^2
$$

where $C_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx 418.4 J/K + C_{\mathrm{cup}} \approx 435 J/K$, $\tau = C_{\mathrm{eff}}/G_{\mathrm{loss}} \approx 900–1400 s$, $s_{\mathrm{strat}} = \mathrm{TG}_{\mathrm{top}}/\mathrm{TG}_{\mathrm{bulk}} \approx 1.25\text{--}1.38$ (top-layer stratification factor), and $\Delta T_{\mathrm{cool}} \approx (0.012 °C/s)\,t_{\mathrm{wait}}$ is post-lamp cooling during cup removal.\\
**2. Official 2027 Scoring & Penalty Stacking (**[2027-RULE]** 6.c–h & Scoresheet v2.0.0):**

$$
\mathrm{FS} = \mathrm{ES} + \mathrm{TS} + \mathrm{PS}\ (\max 100),\quad
  \mathrm{ES} = 50\frac{S_{\mathrm{exam}}}{S_{\mathrm{exam,max}}},\quad
  \mathrm{TS} = 30\frac{\mathrm{TG}_{\mathrm{adj}}}{\mathrm{TG}_{\mathrm{adj,max}}},\quad
  \mathrm{PS} = 20\frac{\mathrm{PE}_{\mathrm{adj}}}{\mathrm{PE}_{\mathrm{adj,max}}},\quad
  \mathrm{TG} = \max(0, T_f - T_i),\quad
  \mathrm{PE} = \max\!\left(0,\,1 - \frac{|T_f - T_{\mathrm{pred}}|}{T_f}\right)
$$

where $\mathrm{TG}_{\mathrm{adj}} = \mathrm{TG}\times 0.7^{N_{\mathrm{constr}}}\times 0.9^{N_{\mathrm{comp}}}$ and $\mathrm{PE}_{\mathrm{adj}} = \mathrm{PE}\times 0.7^{N_{\mathrm{constr}}}\times 0.9^{N_{\mathrm{comp}}}$. **CRITICAL:** $T_f$ in the $\mathrm{PE}$ denominator is in **degrees Celsius** (**[2027-RULE]** 6.b)!

Note: **Julius Robert von Mayer** proposed conservation of energy earlier (1842, from blood oxidation), leading to the Mayer–Joule priority dispute. |

Note: the phrase “ultraviolet catastrophe” was coined by **Paul Ehrenfest** in 1911, not Planck. |

Rudolf Clausius** | 1822–1888 (K\"oslin, Prussia $\to$ Zurich / Bonn) | *On the Moving Force of Heat* (1850); *Mechanical Theory of Heat* (1865) | Reconciled Carnot's principle with Joule's energy conservation (1850); **coined “entropy” $S$** ($dS = \delta Q_{\mathrm{rev}}/T$, 1865, from Greek *trope* = transformation); **Clausius inequality** $\oint \delta Q/T \le 0$; Clausius–Clapeyron eq.; virial theorem. | Famous 1865 couplet: *“The energy of the universe is constant. The entropy of the universe tends to a maximum.”* Introduced mean free path $\lambda$ (1858). |
| **7. Ludwig Boltzmann** | 1844–1906 (Vienna $\to$ Graz / Vienna) | *Thermal Equilibrium of Gas Molecules* (1872); *Probabilistic 2nd Law* (1877) | Founded statistical mechanics; statistical entropy $\mathbf{S = k \log W}$ (engraved on Vienna tombstone; explicitly written in that constant form by Planck, 1900); **$H$-theorem** | PhD advisor was **Josef Stefan**; Boltzmann derived the $T^4$ radiation law theoretically from Maxwell's electrodynamics in 1884 (Stefan found it empirically in 1879). |
| **8. James Clerk Maxwell** | 1831–1879 (Edinburgh $\to$ King's / Cambridge) | *Dynamical Theory of Gases* (1860, 1866); *Theory of Heat* (1871) | Derived **Maxwell speed distribution** $f(v)$ (1860); proved gas viscosity $\mu$ is *independent of pressure/density* (confirmed experimentally with Katherine Mary Clerk Maxwell, 1866); **4 Maxwell relations**; **Maxwell's demon** (1867/1871). | First Cavendish Professor at Cambridge (1871). Maxwell's demon was later resolved via information entropy by **Szilard** (1929), **Brillouin**, and **Landauer** ($k_B T\ln 2$ erasure cost, 1961). |

| $\Delta U = q + w_{\mathrm{on}}$ | $w_{\mathrm{on}} = -W_{\mathrm{by}}$: work done **on** system $(J)$; $q = Q$: heat added **to** system $(J)$ | **[CLOSED]** | Chemistry / IUPAC convention translation ($w_{\mathrm{on}} = -P_{\mathrm{ext}}\Delta V$) **[S16]** |

| $y = y_1 + (y_2 - y_1)\dfrac{x - x_1}{x_2 - x_1}$ | $(x_1, y_1), (x_2, y_2)$: adjacent table rows; $x$: target state; $y$: interpolated property | **[2027-RULE]** | Linear table interpolation (steam tables, DOE bulb-height lookup) **[S09,S16]** |

## System Boundaries, Control Volumes & The Locked Sign Contract

Every thermodynamic calculation begins by drawing an explicit **system boundary** (real or imaginary surface) separating the **system** from its **surroundings** (Fig. `fig:02:boundaries`)  **[S12,S13,S16]**. Sign errors and missing energy terms in written exams almost always trace to an unstated or shifting boundary.

> **[Vector Figure: System classification and boundary ledger under the locked Physics sign convention ($\Delta U = Q - W_{\mathrm{by}}$). Choosing a closed vs. open boundary determines whether flow work $Pv$ is tracked separately or bundled into enthalpy $H = U + PV$  **[S12,S13,S16]**. | Label: `fig:02:boundaries`]**
> - **Diagram Annotations & Key Elements:** 1. CLOSED SYSTEM (Control Mass) • Fixed mass $m = \mathrm{const}$ ($\Delta m = 0$) / Impermeable boundary ($\dot{m}=0$) / $\Delta U = Q - W_{\mathrm{by}} = Q + W_{\mathrm{on}}$ • (heat in) • (work out) • Ex: Sealed piston–cylinder, sealed / gas tank, covered non-evaporating cup • 2. OPEN SYSTEM (Control Volume) • Mass crosses boundary ($\dot{m}_{\mathrm{in}}, \dot{m}_{\mathrm{out}} \neq 0$) / Carries enthalpy $h = u + Pv$ / Steady: $\dot{Q} - \dot{W}_s = \dot{m}(h_{\mathrm{out}} - h_{\mathrm{in}})$ • Ex: Uncovered evaporating 9 oz cup, / turbine, compressor, throttling valve • 3. ISOLATED SYSTEM • $\Delta m = 0, \quad Q = 0, \quad W = 0$ / $\Delta U_{\mathrm{iso}} = \sum \Delta U_i = 0$ / $\Delta S_{\mathrm{iso}} = S_{\mathrm{gen}} \geq 0$ • Ex: Ideal sealed calorimeter / (cup + contents), the Universe

### Boundary Constraint Pairs

Every physical wall or interface in a competition problem enforces a mathematical constraint:
- **Adiabatic vs. Diathermal Boundary:** An *adiabatic* wall prevents heat transfer ($Q = 0$ or $\dot{Q} = 0$; realized by vacuum jacketing, thick low-$k$ insulation, or an acoustic/rapid process where $t_{\mathrm{proc}} \ll \tau_{\mathrm{th}}$). A *diathermal* wall conducts heat freely so separated subsystems equilibrate to a shared temperature $T_A = T_B$  **[S13,S16]**.
- **Rigid vs. Movable/Deformable Boundary:** A *rigid* vessel has fixed volume ($\Delta V = 0 \implies W_{\mathrm{by,boundary}} = \int P\,dV = 0$), though shaft/paddle-wheel or electrical work ($W_{\mathrm{elec}} = -VIt$) may still cross the wall. A *freely movable frictionless piston* of mass $m_p$ and area $A_p$ enforces constant internal pressure $P_{\mathrm{gas}} = P_{\mathrm{atm}} + m_p g / A_p$ (isobaric process)  **[S13]**.
- **Impermeable vs. Permeable/Open Boundary:** An uncovered 9 oz cup of warm water under the 2027 heat lamp is an *open system* because water vapor crosses the top free surface ($\dot{m}_{\mathrm{evap}} > 0$), carrying away latent enthalpy $\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{evap}} = \dot{m}_{\mathrm{evap}} L_v$  **[S01,S12]**. Placing an unattached clear BoPET film cap over the rim (`Clarification #5`) converts the cup into a *closed system* ($\dot{m}_{\mathrm{evap}} \approx 0$)  **[S02]**.

### First Law Sign Convention Lock & Physics-to-Chemistry Translation

In physics and mechanical engineering textbooks (OpenStax *University Physics Vol. 2*, Lienhard 6e, MIT 2.005/16.Unified)  **[S12,S13]**, thermodynamic engines are primary, so expansion work done **by** the gas is defined as positive ($W_{\mathrm{by}} > 0$) and subtracted from heat added ($\Delta U = Q - W_{\mathrm{by}}$). In chemistry textbooks (IUPAC, MIT 5.60)  **[S16]**, all energy entering the system is defined as positive, so compression work done **on** the gas is positive ($w_{\mathrm{on}} > 0$) and added to heat ($\Delta U = q + w_{\mathrm{on}}$). Both conventions yield the **exact same physical $\Delta U$** because $W_{\mathrm{on}} = -W_{\mathrm{by}}$ (Table `tab:02:signtrans`).

**Table:** Complete Physics ($\Delta U = Q - W_{\mathrm{by}}$) vs. Chemistry/IUPAC ($\Delta U = Q + W_{\mathrm{on}}$) sign translation across all 11 canonical processes  **[S13,S16]**.

| **Process / Physical Action** | $\boldsymbol{\Delta V}$ | **Heat $\boldsymbol{Q}$** | **Physics $\boldsymbol{W_{\mathrm{by}}}$** | **Chem $\boldsymbol{W_{\mathrm{on}}}$** | **Internal Energy Change $\boldsymbol{\Delta U}$ (Identical in Both!)** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Isochoric heating (rigid tank) | $0$ | $>0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $\Delta U = +Q = +nC_{V,m}\Delta T > 0$ ($\Delta T > 0$) |
| 2. Isochoric cooling (rigid tank) | $0$ | $<0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $\Delta U = Q = nC_{V,m}\Delta T < 0$ ($\Delta T < 0$) |
| 3. Isobaric expansion ($P=\mathrm{const}$) | $>0$ | $+nC_{P,m}\Delta T > 0$ | $+P\Delta V > 0$ | $-P\Delta V < 0$ | $\Delta U = Q - P\Delta V = +nC_{V,m}\Delta T > 0$ |
| 4. Isobaric compression ($P=\mathrm{const}$) | $<0$ | $nC_{P,m}\Delta T < 0$ | $P\Delta V < 0$ | $-P\Delta V > 0$ | $\Delta U = Q - P\Delta V = nC_{V,m}\Delta T < 0$ |
| 5. Isothermal expansion (ideal gas) | $>0$ | $+nRT\ln(V_2/V_1) > 0$ | $+nRT\ln(V_2/V_1) > 0$ | $-nRT\ln(V_2/V_1) < 0$ | $\Delta U = 0 \implies Q = W_{\mathrm{by}} = -W_{\mathrm{on}} > 0$ |
| 6. Isothermal compression (ideal gas) | $<0$ | $nRT\ln(V_2/V_1) < 0$ | $nRT\ln(V_2/V_1) < 0$ | $-nRT\ln(V_2/V_1) > 0$ | $\Delta U = 0 \implies Q = W_{\mathrm{by}} = -W_{\mathrm{on}} < 0$ |
| 7. Adiabatic expansion ($Q=0$) | $>0$ | $0$ | $+\dfrac{P_1V_1-P_2V_2}{\gamma-1} > 0$ | $-\dfrac{P_1V_1-P_2V_2}{\gamma-1} < 0$ | $\Delta U = -W_{\mathrm{by}} = +W_{\mathrm{on}} < 0$ (gas cools, $\Delta T < 0$) |
| 8. Adiabatic compression ($Q=0$) | $<0$ | $0$ | $\dfrac{P_1V_1-P_2V_2}{\gamma-1} < 0$ | $-\dfrac{P_1V_1-P_2V_2}{\gamma-1} > 0$ | $\Delta U = -W_{\mathrm{by}} = +W_{\mathrm{on}} > 0$ (gas warms, $\Delta T > 0$) |
| 9. Free expansion into vacuum ($P_{\mathrm{ext}}=0$) | $>0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $\Delta U = 0$ ($\Delta T = 0$ for ideal gas; $\Delta S = nR\ln(V_2/V_1) > 0$) |
| 10. Clockwise $P$–$V$ cycle (heat engine) | $0_{\mathrm{cyc}}$ | $Q_H - Q_C > 0$ | $+\mathrm{Area} > 0$ | $-\mathrm{Area} < 0$ | $\Delta U_{\mathrm{cycle}} = 0 \implies W_{\mathrm{net,by}} = Q_H - Q_C > 0$ |
| 11. Counterclockwise $P$–$V$ cycle (refrig.) | $0_{\mathrm{cyc}}$ | $Q_C - Q_H < 0$ | $-\mathrm{Area} < 0$ | $+\mathrm{Area} > 0$ | $\Delta U_{\mathrm{cycle}} = 0 \implies W_{\mathrm{in}} = W_{\mathrm{net,on}} = Q_H - Q_C > 0$ |

## Symbol Disambiguation & Dimensional Consistency

Thermodynamics reuses several Latin and Greek letters for unrelated physical quantities with different dimensions. Before substituting numbers into any formula, check the symbol's **subscript and SI unit** (Table `tab:02:symcollision`).

**Table:** High-risk symbol collisions in thermodynamics and heat transfer: how to disambiguate by context and SI units  **[S07,S12,S13]**.

| **Overloaded Letter** | **Distinct Symbols** | **SI Units** | **Physical Meaning & Disambiguation Rule** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| \multirow{3}{*}{$Q,\ \dot{Q},\ q,\ q''$} | $Q$ | $J$ | Total thermal energy transferred across boundary during a finite time interval $\Delta t$ |
|  | $\dot{Q} = Q/t$ | $W = J/s$ | Heat transfer rate (thermal power); integrate/multiply by time $t$ $(s)$ to get $Q$ $(J)$ |
|  | $q = Q/m$ vs. $q'' = \dot{Q}/A$ | $J/kg$ vs. $W/m^2$ | Mass-specific heat transfer $q$ $(J/kg)$ vs. heat flux $q''$ (power per unit area, $W/m^2$) |
| \multirow{3}{*}{$c,\ C,\ C_m$} | $c,\ c_p,\ c_v$ | $J/kg/K$ (or $J/g/K$) | Mass-specific heat capacity (intensive; $1\,J/g/K = 1000 J/kg/K$) |
|  | $C = mc = nC_m$ | $J/K$ | Total heat capacity of an object or calorimeter $C_{\mathrm{cal}}$ (extensive!) |
|  | $C_m = Mc,\ C_{P,m},\ C_{V,m}$ | $J/mol/K$ | Molar heat capacity (intensive; $C_{P,m} - C_{V,m} = R = 8.31446 J/mol/K$ for ideal gas) |
| \multirow{3}{*}{$R,\ R_s,\ R_{\mathrm{th}},\ R_{\mathrm{val}}$} | $R = N_A k_B$ vs. $R_s = R/M$ | $J/mol/K$ vs. $J/kg/K$ | Universal molar gas constant ($8.31446 J/mol/K$) vs. specific gas constant ($R_{\mathrm{air}} = 287.05 J/kg/K$) |
|  | $R_{\mathrm{th}} = \Delta T / \dot{Q}$ | $K/W$ | Lumped thermal resistance ($L/(kA)$ for conduction, $1/(hA)$ for convection) |
|  | $R_{\mathrm{val}} = R'' = L/k$ | $m^2 K/W$ | Unit-area thermal insulance ($R$-value; $R_{\mathrm{th}} = R_{\mathrm{val}}/A$) |
| \multirow{3}{*}{$\alpha_L,\ \alpha_{\mathrm{diff}},\ \alpha_{\mathrm{rad}}$} | $\alpha_L = \frac{1}{L}\frac{\Delta L}{\Delta T}$ | $/K$ (or $/°C$) | Linear coefficient of thermal expansion ($\beta_V \approx 3\alpha_L$ for isotropic solids) |
|  | $\alpha = k/(\rho c_p)$ | $m^2/s$ | Thermal diffusivity (rate of transient thermal penetration; enters Fourier number $\mathrm{Fo} = \alpha t/L_c^2$) |
|  | $\alpha,\ \alpha_\lambda$ | dimensionless $\in [0,1]$ | Hemispherical radiative absorptivity ($\alpha + \rho + \tau = 1$; equals $\varepsilon_\lambda$ at equilibrium) |
| \multirow{2}{*}{$h,\ h_{\mathrm{conv}},\ h_{\mathrm{plank}}$} | $h = u + Pv$ vs. $h_{\mathrm{conv}}$ | $J/kg$ vs. $W/m^2/K$ | Specific enthalpy $h$ ($H/m$) vs. convective heat transfer coefficient $h$ ($\dot{Q} = hA\Delta T$) |
|  | $h$ (Planck) vs. $h_{\mathrm{bulb}}$ | $J s$ vs. $cm$ or $m$ | Planck constant ($6.62607015×10^{-34} J s$) vs. 2027 heat-lamp bulb height ($40–65 cm$) |
| \multirow{2}{*}{$k_B,\ k_{\mathrm{cond}},\ \gamma$} | $k_B$ vs. $k$ | $J/K$ vs. $W/m/K$ | Boltzmann constant ($1.380649×10^{-23} J/K$) vs. thermal conductivity ($\dot{Q} = kA\Delta T/L$) |
|  | $\gamma = C_P/C_V$ | dimensionless $>1$ | Adiabatic index / heat-capacity ratio ($\tfrac{5}{3}$ monatomic, $\tfrac{7}{5}$ diatomic, $\tfrac{4}{3}$ nonlinear polyatomic) |

## SI Base Units, Exact 2019 SI Definitions & Multi-Unit Conversion Matrix

Since May 20, 2019 (9th SI Brochure / NIST CODATA 2022)  **[S07,S08]**, all seven SI base units are defined by fixing exact numerical values of fundamental constants:
- **The Kelvin ($K$):** Defined by fixing the Boltzmann constant to **exactly** $k_B = 1.380649×10^{-23} J/K$ ($kg m^2/s^2/K$). A change of $1 K$ corresponds to a thermal energy scale shift $\Delta(k_B T) = 1.380649×10^{-23} J$. Consequently, the triple point of water ($T_{\mathrm{tp}} = 273.16 K = 0.01 °C$ at $P_{\mathrm{tp}} = 611.657 Pa$) is now an experimentally measured quantity with a relative standard uncertainty of $1.5×10^{-7}$ ($\pm0.0001 K$), whereas the Celsius offset $T(°C) = T(K) - 273.15$ remains exact  **[S07,S08]**.
- **The Mole ($mol$) & Universal Gas Constant ($R$):** Fixing Avogadro's constant to **exactly** $N_A = 6.02214076×10^{23} /mol$ makes the molar gas constant $R = N_A k_B$ an **exact 23-digit decimal**:
  
$$
\begin{aligned}

  \begin{aligned}
    R = N_A k_B &= 8.31446261815324 J/mol/K = 8.314462618 Pa m^3/mol/K = 8.314462618 L kPa/mol/K \\
      &= 0.08314462618 L bar/mol/K = 0.08205736608 L \,atm/mol/K = 62.36359822 L \,Torr/mol/K \\
      &= 1.987204259 cal_{ th }/mol/K = 8.314462618×10^{7} erg/mol/K = 1.985875\ \mathrm{BTU_{IT}/(lbmol\cdot{^\circ R})}.
  \end{aligned}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Table:** Verified NIST CODATA 2022 & NIST SP 811 conversion factors for competition calculations  **[S07,S08]**.

| **Dimension** | **Coherent SI Unit** | **Exact or NIST SP 811 Conversion Factors** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Energy / Heat / Work** | $1 J = 1 N m = 1 Pa m^3$ | $1\,\mathrm{cal_{th}} = 4.184 J$ (exact); $1\,\mathrm{cal_{IT}} = 4.1868 J$ (exact); $1\,\mathrm{Cal}$ (dietary) $= 1\,\mathrm{kcal_{th}} = 4184 J$; $1\,\mathrm{BTU_{IT}} = 1055.05585262 J = 251.9958 cal_{IT} = 778.16926 ft · lbf$; $1\,\mathrm{BTU_{th}} = 1054.3503 J$; $1 L \,atm = 101.325 J$ (exact); $1 L bar = 100 J$ (exact); $1 L kPa = 1 J$ (exact); $1 kW h = 3.6×10^{6} J$ (exact); $1\,\mathrm{therm\ (US)} = 10^5\,\mathrm{BTU} = 1.054804×10^{8} J$; $1\,\mathrm{erg} = 10^{-7} J$; $1 eV = 1.602176634×10^{-19} J$ |
| **Power / Heat Rate** | $1 W = 1 J/s$ | $1\,\mathrm{BTU_{IT}/h} = 0.29307107 W$; $1\,\mathrm{BTU_{IT}/s} = 1055.0559 W$; $1\,\mathrm{ton\ of\ refrigeration} = 200\,\mathrm{BTU_{IT}/min} = 12000 BTU_{IT}/h = 3516.8528 W \approx 3.517 kW$; $1\,\mathrm{hp\ (mech)} = 550 ft · lbf/s = 745.69987 W$ |
| **Pressure** | $1 Pa = 1 N/m^2 = 1 J/m^3$ | $1 atm = 101325 Pa = 101.325 kPa = 1.01325 bar = 760\,\mathrm{Torr} = 760 mmHg\ (0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}) = 14.6959488 psi = 29.92126 inHg = 10.33227 mH_2O\ (4\,^\circ\mathrm{C})$; $1 bar = 10^{5} Pa = 100 kPa = 0.98692327 atm = 14.5037738 psi$; $1\,\mathrm{Torr} = \frac{101325}{760}\,Pa = 133.3223684 Pa$; $1\,\mathrm{psi} = 6894.757293 Pa$; $1\,\mathrm{inH_2O}\ (4\,^\circ\mathrm{C}) = 249.0889 Pa$ |
| **Specific Heat Capacity** | $1 J/kg/K = 1 J/kg/°C$ | $1 J/g/K = 1 kJ/kg/K = 1000 J/kg/K$; $1\,\mathrm{cal_{th}/(g\cdot^\circ C)} = 4184 J/kg/K$; $1\,\mathrm{cal_{IT}/(g\cdot^\circ C)} = 1\,\mathrm{BTU_{IT}/(lbm\cdot^\circ F)} = 4186.8 J/kg/K$ (exact) |

| **Thermal Conductivity** | $1 W/m/K$ | $1\,\mathrm{BTU_{IT}/(h\cdot ft\cdot^\circ F)} = 1.730735 W/m/K$; $1\,\mathrm{BTU_{IT}\cdot in/(h\cdot ft^2\cdot^\circ F)} = 0.1442279 W/m/K$; $1\,\mathrm{cal_{th}/(s\cdot cm\cdot^\circ C)} = 418.4 W/m/K$ |
| **Conductance / $R$-Value** | $h, U$: $W/m^2/K$; $R''$: $m^2 K/W$ | $1\,\mathrm{BTU_{IT}/(h\cdot ft^2\cdot^\circ F)} = 5.678263 W/m^2/K$; $1\,\text{R-value (US: }\mathrm{h\cdot ft^2\cdot^\circ F/BTU_{IT}}\text{)} = 0.17611018 m^2 K/W$ (RSI); $1\,\mathrm{RSI} = 5.678263\,\text{R-value (US)}$; $1\,\mathrm{clo} = 0.155 m^2 K/W$ |

### STP vs. SATP Molar Volume Disambiguation

Never assume “STP” means $22.4 L/mol$ without checking the pressure standard  **[S07]**:
- **IUPAC / Modern NIST STP ($T = 273.15 K = 0 °C$, $P = 1 bar = 100 kPa$):** $V_m = RT/P = \mathbf{22.71095 L/mol}$ ($n_0 = 2.651646×10^{25} /m^3$).
- **Traditional / US Textbook STP ($T = 273.15 K = 0 °C$, $P = 1 atm = 101.325 kPa$):** $V_m = RT/P = \mathbf{22.41397 L/mol}$ ($n_0 = 2.686780×10^{25} /m^3$).
- **SATP (Standard Ambient $T = 298.15 K = 25 °C$, $P = 1 bar = 100 kPa$):** $V_m = \mathbf{24.78957 L/mol}$ (or $\mathbf{24.46540 L/mol}$ at $25 °C, 1 atm$).

## Science Olympiad Significant Figures & Rounding Policy

Rule `5.I.b` requires all written answers to be reported in **metric units with appropriate significant figures unless otherwise specified**  **[S01,S06]**:
- **Measurement Recording Rule:** Record all certain digits from instrument graduations plus **one (and only one) estimated digit** (typically $\pm 0.1$ of the smallest graduation for analog scales, or the last displayed digit on a digital thermometer)  **[S06]**. Under 2027 Rules `4.f` and `5.II.c,g`, the ES thermometer reads to $\mathbf{0.1 °C}$ (e.g., $21.4 °C$ has 3 sig figs and 1 decimal place)  **[S01]**.
- **Addition & Subtraction (Decimal-Place Rule):** Round the result to the **least precise decimal column** among the terms.
- *Critical Calorimetry & Temperature-Convert Trap:* Converting $T_C = 25.0 °C$ (1 decimal place, 3 sig figs) to kelvin via $T_K = 25.0 + 273.15 = 298.15 K \to \mathbf{298.2 K}$ limits the kelvin value to **1 decimal place (4 sig figs)**. Conversely, subtracting two close thermometer readings $T_f - T_i = 28.4\,°C - 22.7\,°C = \mathbf{5.7 °C}$ preserves 1 decimal place but drops from 3 sig figs to **2 sig figs** (limiting $Q = mc\Delta T$ to 2 sig figs!).
- **Multiplication, Division, Powers & Roots (Sig-Fig Count Rule):** Round the final answer to the **smallest number of significant figures** among any measured factor. Defined exact constants ($k_B, N_A, R, 4.184 J /cal_{th}, 101325 Pa /atm$, stoichiometric integers, $\tfrac{3}{2}, \tfrac{5}{2}$) have **infinite significant figures** and never limit precision  **[S06,S07]**.
- **Logarithms & Exponentials ($\ln x$, $\log_{10} x$, $e^x$):** In $y = \ln x$ or $\log_{10} x$, the number of digits after the decimal point in $y$ (the *mantissa*) equals the number of significant figures in $x$ (e.g., $\ln(2.50) = 0.91629\ldots \to \mathbf{0.916}$ has 3 decimal places because $2.50$ has 3 sig figs). In $x = e^y$ or $10^y$, the number of sig figs in $x$ equals the number of decimal places in $y$  **[S06]**.
- **Guard-Digit Rule:** Never round intermediate values during multi-step calculations! Store full floating-point precision in your Class III calculator memory (`STO`/`ANS`) and round **only the final reported number**  **[S06]**.

## Rule `5.d.i–iv` Algebra-Only & Geometry-Only Math Toolkit

### [2027 OFFICIAL RULE / CLARIFICATION: 2027 Rule 5.d.i–iv & National Physics Math Guidelines  **[S01,S06]**]
- **Permitted Mathematics (`5.d.i–iii`):** Arithmetic (ratios, scientific notation, exponents, roots, absolute values), algebraic manipulations (multi-step and multi-variable symbolic derivations, linear systems, quadratics, logarithms $\ln/\log_{10}$ and exponentials $e^x$ per `MathGuidelines2022.pdf` Division C Algebra II), and geometry (areas and volumes of rectangles, triangles, trapezoids, circles/ellipses, cylinders, spheres, cones, and cubes).
- **Strict Prohibition (`5.d.iv`):** *“No questions may require trigonometry or calculus.”* Every problem on a 2027 compliant exam can be solved without differentiation, integration, or trigonometric functions ($\sin, \cos, \tan$).

### How Calculus-Origin Formulas Reduce to Pure Algebra & Geometry
- **$P$–$V$ Work as Geometric Area (`5.d.iii`):** Instead of evaluating $\int_{V_1}^{V_2} P(V)\,dV$, identify the geometric shape under the path on the $P$–$V$ plane (remembering $1 kPa\times1 L = 1 J$ and $1 MPa\times1 m^3 = 1 MJ$):
- *Isochoric vertical line ($V_2 = V_1$):* Base width is zero $\implies W_{\mathrm{by}} = 0$.
- *Isobaric horizontal line ($P = \mathrm{const}$):* Rectangle of height $P$ and width $(V_2 - V_1) \implies W_{\mathrm{by}} = P(V_2 - V_1)$.
- *Straight-line segment from $(V_1, P_1)$ to $(V_2, P_2)$:* Trapezoid of average height $\bar{P} = \tfrac{1}{2}(P_1 + P_2) \implies W_{\mathrm{by}} = \tfrac{1}{2}(P_1 + P_2)(V_2 - V_1)$.
- *Closed cycle (polygon or ellipse):* Net work per cycle is the **enclosed area** ($+\mathrm{Area}$ if clockwise, $-\mathrm{Area}$ if counterclockwise):
        
$$
\begin{aligned}

          W_{\mathrm{rect}} = \Delta P\,\Delta V, \qquad W_{\mathrm{triangle}} = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\Delta P\,\Delta V, \qquad W_{\mathrm{ellipse/circle}} = \pi a b = \frac{\pi}{4}(P_{\max} - P_{\min})(V_{\max} - V_{\min}).
\end{aligned}
$$
- **Zero-Calculus Proof of Reversible Adiabatic Work:** For an ideal gas, internal energy is a state function that always satisfies $\Delta U = nC_{V,m}(T_2 - T_1) = \frac{nR(T_2 - T_1)}{\gamma - 1} = \frac{P_2V_2 - P_1V_1}{\gamma - 1}$ regardless of path. Setting $Q = 0$ in the First Law $\Delta U = Q - W_{\mathrm{by}}$ immediately yields $W_{\mathrm{by}} = -\Delta U = \dfrac{P_1V_1 - P_2V_2}{\gamma - 1}$ by pure algebra without integrating $PV^\gamma$!
- **Closed-Form Logarithmic Formulas (Direct Calculator `LN` Key):** For reversible isothermal work $W_{\mathrm{by}} = nRT\ln(V_2/V_1)$, constant-$c$ warming entropy $\Delta S = mc\ln(T_2/T_1)$, ideal-gas entropy $\Delta S = nC_{V,m}\ln(T_2/T_1) + nR\ln(V_2/V_1)$, and cylindrical conduction resistance $R_{\mathrm{cyl}} = \frac{\ln(r_o/r_i)}{2\pi k L}$, substitute the dimensionless ratio directly into the $\ln(\cdot)$ key on your Class III calculator.
- **Logarithmic Mean Temperature Difference (LMTD) & Thin-Annulus Approximations:** When $r_o/r_i = 1 + \epsilon$ with $|\epsilon| \ll 1$, the algebraic Padé approximation $\ln\left(\frac{r_o}{r_i}\right) \approx \frac{r_o - r_i}{(r_o + r_i)/2} = \frac{\Delta r}{r_{\mathrm{avg}}}$ reduces cylindrical conduction to a flat slab of mean area $A_{\mathrm{avg}} = 2\pi r_{\mathrm{avg}} L$ to within $<0.1\%$ for $\epsilon < 0.05$.
- **Pythagorean Aspect-Ratio Replacement for Sloped Reflectors (Zero Trigonometry!):** For a truncated conical reflector of top radius $R_1$, bottom radius $R_2$, and vertical height $H$, never use $\sin\theta$ or $\cos\theta$; use the slant length $s = \sqrt{H^2 + (R_1 - R_2)^2}$, lateral surface area $A_{\mathrm{lat}} = \pi(R_1 + R_2)\sqrt{H^2 + (R_1 - R_2)^2}$, and frustum volume $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi H(R_1^2 + R_1 R_2 + R_2^2)$  **[S01]**.

## Layered Worked Examples & Diagnostics

### Worked Example — First Law Sign Translation & Multi-Unit Pressure-Volume Work `[Basic $\cdot$ Rule 5.c.i, 5.c.iv]`

A closed piston–cylinder assembly contains a gas that expands at a constant external pressure of $P = 2.50 atm$ from an initial volume of $V_1 = 1.20 L$ to a final volume of $V_2 = 4.80 L$ while absorbing $Q = 350.0 cal_{th}$ of heat from a heater. Find (a) the boundary work in joules under both the Physics ($W_{\mathrm{by}}$) and Chemistry ($w_{\mathrm{on}}$) conventions, and (b) the internal energy change $\Delta U$ in joules.

**Solution.**
**(a)** Convert heat and pressure–volume units to coherent SI ($J$):

$$
Q = 350.0 cal_{th} \times 4.184 J /cal_{th} = +1464.4 J, \qquad
  P\Delta V = (2.50 atm)(4.80 - 1.20 L) = 9.00 L \,atm.
$$

Using the exact conversion $1 L \,atm = 101.325 J$:

$$
W_{\mathrm{by}} = +P\Delta V = 9.00 \times 101.325 J = \mathbf{+911.925 J \approx +912 J}, \qquad
  w_{\mathrm{on}} = -W_{\mathrm{by}} = \mathbf{-911.925 J \approx -912 J}.
$$

**(b)** Internal energy change is identical under both conventions:

$$
\Delta U = Q - W_{\mathrm{by}} = 1464.4 - 911.925 = \mathbf{+552.475 J \approx +552 J} \quad (\text{or } \Delta U = q + w_{\mathrm{on}} = 1464.4 + (-911.925) = +552.475 J).
$$

**✓ Verified by:** Direct SI conversion: $P = 2.50 \times 101325 Pa = 253312.5 Pa$, $\Delta V = 3.60×10^{-3} m^3 \implies W_{\mathrm{by}} = 911.925 J$, $\Delta U = 552.475 J$ (`check_sec02_05.py`).

### Worked Example — Geometric $P$–$V$ Cycle Area & Significant Figures Trap `[Competition $\cdot$ Rules 5.I.b, 5.d.iii]`

An ideal gas executes a clockwise right-triangular cycle $A \to B \to C \to A$ on a $P$–$V$ diagram with vertices $A(2.00 L, 100.0 kPa)$, $B(8.00 L, 400.0 kPa)$ along a straight chord, $C(8.00 L, 100.0 kPa)$ isochorically, and $C \to A$ isobarically. Compute (a) the work $W_{\mathrm{by}}$ along each leg $A\to B$, $B\to C$, and $C\to A$, and (b) the net work $W_{\mathrm{net}}$ and net heat $Q_{\mathrm{net}}$ over the complete cycle.

**Solution.**
**(a)** Recall $1 kPa\times1 L = 1 J$:
- Leg $A \to B$ (straight-line expansion from $V_A = 2.00 L$ to $V_B = 8.00 L$): Trapezoid area under segment $AB$:
    
$$
W_{A\to B} = \tfrac{1}{2}(P_A + P_B)(V_B - V_A) = \tfrac{1}{2}(100.0 + 400.0 kPa)(8.00 - 2.00 L) = (250.0 kPa)(6.00 L) = \mathbf{+1500 J = +1.50 kJ}.
$$
- Leg $B \to C$ (isochoric cooling at $V = 8.00 L$): $\Delta V = 0 \implies W_{B\to C} = \mathbf{0 J}$.
- Leg $C \to A$ (isobaric compression at $P = 100.0 kPa$ from $8.00 L$ to $2.00 L$): Rectangle area moving left:
    
$$
W_{C\to A} = P_C(V_A - V_C) = (100.0 kPa)(2.00 - 8.00 L) = \mathbf{-600 J = -0.600 kJ}.
$$

**(b)** Over the closed cycle, $\Delta U_{\mathrm{cycle}} = 0$, so $Q_{\mathrm{net}} = W_{\mathrm{net}} = W_{A\to B} + W_{B\to C} + W_{C\to A} = 1500 + 0 - 600 = \mathbf{+900 J = +0.900 kJ}$ (3 sig figs, limited by $\Delta V = 6.00 L$).

**✓ Verified by:** Right-triangle enclosed area formula: $W_{\mathrm{net}} = +\tfrac{1}{2}\Delta V\,\Delta P = \tfrac{1}{2}(6.00 L)(300.0 kPa) = +900.0 J$ (`check_sec02_05.py`).

### Worked Example — Compound Imperial-to-SI Conversion: Refrigeration Tonnage & Thermal Resistance `[Competition $\cdot$ Rule 5.c.i, 5.c.iii]`

A cold-storage room has walls of total area $A = 45.0 m^2$ insulated to a US rating of $\text{R-}19$ ($19.0 h · ft^2 ·^\circ F/BTU_{IT}$). When the outside air is $95.0 ^\circ F$ and the inside room is held at $23.0 ^\circ F$, find (a) the SI unit-area insulance $R_{\mathrm{val}}$ ($m^2 K/W$) and total thermal resistance $R_{\mathrm{th}}$ ($K/W$), and (b) the steady conductive heat leak $\dot{Q}$ in watts and in tons of refrigeration.

**Solution.**
**(a)** From Table `tab:02:conversions`, $1\,\text{R-value (US)} = 0.17611018 m^2 K/W$:

$$
R_{\mathrm{val}} = 19.0 \times 0.17611018 m^2 K/W = \mathbf{3.346 m^2 K/W}, \qquad
  R_{\mathrm{th}} = \frac{R_{\mathrm{val}}}{A} = \frac{3.3461 m^2 K/W}{45.0 m^2} = \mathbf{0.07436 K/W}.
$$

**(b)** Convert the temperature difference using the interval ratio $\Delta T_K = \Delta T_C = \frac{5}{9}\Delta T_F$ (do NOT subtract $32$ from $\Delta T_F$!):

$$
\Delta T_F = 95.0 - 23.0 = 72.0 ^\circ F \implies \Delta T_K = \frac{5}{9}(72.0) = 40.0 K.
$$

The steady heat leak is:

$$
\dot{Q} = \frac{\Delta T_K}{R_{\mathrm{th}}} = \frac{40.0 K}{0.074358 K/W} = \mathbf{537.9 W \approx 538 W}, \qquad
  \dot{Q}_{\mathrm{tons}} = \frac{537.94 W}{3516.85 W /ton} = \mathbf{0.153 tons\ of\ refrigeration}.
$$

**✓ Verified by:** Direct imperial flux calculation: $A = 45.0 m^2 / (0.3048 m /ft)^2 = 484.376 ft^2$, $\dot{Q} = 484.376 \times 72.0 / 19.0 = 1835.53 BTU_{IT}/h = 0.15296 tons = 537.94 W$ (`check_sec02_05.py`).

### Worked Example — Algebraic Binomial & Linear Interpolation Accuracy Check `[National $\cdot$ Rule 5.d.i–ii]`

(a) Use the NIST saturation water table (Table `tab:02:conversions` / App. A) at $T_1 = 30.0 °C$ ($P_{\mathrm{sat},1} = 4.2470 kPa, L_{v,1} = 2429.8 kJ/kg$) and $T_2 = 35.0 °C$ ($P_{\mathrm{sat},2} = 5.6290 kPa, L_{v,2} = 2417.9 kJ/kg$) to linearly interpolate $P_{\mathrm{sat}}$ and $L_v$ at $T = 32.0 °C$. (b) A copper sphere increases in radius by $\epsilon = \Delta R / R_0 = 1.70×10^{-3}$. Compare the exact fractional volume increase $(1+\epsilon)^3 - 1$ against the binomial linear approximation $3\epsilon$.

**Solution.**
**(a)** The interpolation fraction is $f = (32.0 - 30.0)/(35.0 - 30.0) = 2.0/5.0 = 0.400$:

$$
P_{\mathrm{sat}}(32.0 °C) \approx 4.2470 + 0.400(5.6290 - 4.2470) = \mathbf{4.800 kPa}, \qquad
  L_v(32.0 °C) \approx 2429.8 + 0.400(2417.9 - 2429.8) = \mathbf{2425.0 kJ/kg}.
$$

**(b)** For $\epsilon = 1.70×10^{-3}$:

$$
\left(\frac{\Delta V}{V_0}\right)_{\mathrm{linear}} = 3\epsilon = \mathbf{5.1000×10^{-3}}, \qquad
  \left(\frac{\Delta V}{V_0}\right)_{\mathrm{exact}} = (1.00170)^3 - 1 = \mathbf{5.10867×10^{-3}} \quad (\text{relative error } 0.17\%).
$$

**✓ Verified by:** NIST IAPWS-95 exact evaluation at $32.0 °C$ gives $L_v = 2425.1 kJ/kg$ ($0.004\%$ error) and $P_{\mathrm{sat}} = 4.759 kPa$ ($0.85\%$ secant error) (`check_sec02_05.py`).

### [TRAP & DIAGNOSTIC: §2 Top 5 Sign, Unit & Sig-Fig Traps Diagnosis Table]

| **Wrong move / Symptom** | **What it produces / Why it fails** | **5-second diagnostic & fix** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Using $R = 8.314 J/mol/K$ when $P$ is in $atm$ and $V$ is in $L$ | Off by a factor of $101.325\times$! ($1 L \,atm = 101.325 J$, whereas $1 L kPa = 1 J$) | Either convert $P$ to $kPa$ and $V$ to $L$ (with $R=8.31446$) OR use $R = 0.082057 L \,atm/mol/K$. |
| Using molar mass $M$ in $g/mol$ inside $v_{\mathrm{rms}} = \sqrt{3RT/M}$ or $c_s = \sqrt{\gamma RT/M}$ | Speed is too large by $\sqrt{1000} = 31.62\times$ ($\mathrm{N_2}$ at $300 K$ gives $16340 m/s$ instead of $517 m/s$) | Always convert $M$ to $kg/mol$ ($\mathrm{N_2}: 0.028013 kg/mol$) because $1 J = 1 kg m^2/s^2$. |
| Adding $273.15$ or $32$ when converting a temperature **difference** $\Delta T$ | $\Delta T = 10 °C$ falsely converted to $283.15 K$ or $50 ^\circ F$ | Offset constants cancel in differences: $\Delta T_K = \Delta T_C = \frac{5}{9}\Delta T_F = \frac{5}{4}\Delta T_{\mathrm{R\acute{e}}} = -\frac{2}{3}\Delta T_{\mathrm{De}}$. |
| Mixing Physics $W_{\mathrm{by}}$ and Chemistry $w_{\mathrm{on}}$ in $\Delta U = Q \pm W$ | Sign of work flips, turning $\Delta U = 100 - 40 = 60 J$ into $140 J$ | Ask physically: *Did the gas expand?* Expansion work leaves the gas ($\Delta U$ decreases by $\|W\|$). |
| Using gauge pressure $P_{\mathrm{gauge}}$ instead of $P_{\mathrm{abs}} = P_{\mathrm{gauge}} + P_{\mathrm{atm}}$ in $PV = nRT$ | Fails completely ($P_{\mathrm{gauge}} = 0$ would imply $n=0$ or $T=0$) | Add ambient pressure ($P_{\mathrm{atm}} = 101.325 kPa = 14.696 psi$) before using any gas law or $PV^\gamma$. |

### [2027 HEAT-COLLECTOR DEVICE & LAB: 2027 Heat-Lamp Collector Scoring & Unit Discipline (`Rule 6.a–f`)]

Under 2027 Rule `6.b`, **all Part II device scoring calculations are performed in degrees Celsius ($°C$), NOT kelvin!** Specifically, Temperature Gain is $\mathrm{TG} = T_{\mathrm{final}} - T_{\mathrm{start}}$ (in $°C$) and Prediction Efficiency is:

$$
\mathrm{PE} = \max\!\left(0,\ 1 - \frac{|T_{\mathrm{final}} - T_{\mathrm{pred}}|}{T_{\mathrm{final}}}\right) \quad \text{with } T_{\mathrm{final}} \text{ and } T_{\mathrm{pred}} \text{ in } \mathbf{°C\text{ ( to }0.1 °C\text{)}}  **[S01,S04]**.
$$

Never convert $T_{\mathrm{final}}$ to kelvin inside the denominator of $\mathrm{PE}$, and always submit $T_{\mathrm{pred}}$ in $°C$ rounded to $0.1 °C$ before the end of Heating Time (`Rule 5.II.f`).

—
