## Master Closed-System Process & Thermodynamic Cycle Flash Cards

{**Table:** Master Closed-System Ideal-Gas Process Comparison Flash Card ($n$ moles, $C_{V,m} = \frac{f}{2}R = \frac{R}{\gamma-1}$, $C_{P,m} = \frac{\gamma R}{\gamma-1}$, $\Delta U = Q - W_{\mathrm{by}}$)  **[S13,S25,S30]**.

| **Process** | **Constraint** | **$P, V, T$ Law** | **Work $W_{\mathrm{by}}$ ($=-w_{\mathrm{on}}$)** | **$\Delta U$** | **Heat $Q$ Added** | **$\Delta H$** | **Entropy $\Delta S$ & $PV / TS$ Cues** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Isochoric** (Isometric) | $V = \mathrm{const}$ ($\Delta V = 0$) | $\frac{P_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2}{T_2}$ | $0$ | $nC_{V,m}\Delta T = \frac{V\Delta P}{\gamma-1}$ | $nC_{V,m}\Delta T$ | $nC_{P,m}\Delta T = \gamma\Delta U$ | $\Delta S = nC_{V,m}\ln(T_2/T_1)$; vertical on $PV$; steeper on $TS$ (slope $T/C_V$). |
| **Isobaric** | $P = \mathrm{const}$ ($\Delta P = 0$) | $\frac{V_1}{T_1} = \frac{V_2}{T_2}$ | $P(V_2 - V_1) = nR\Delta T$ | $nC_{V,m}\Delta T = \frac{P\Delta V}{\gamma-1}$ | $nC_{P,m}\Delta T = \frac{\gamma P\Delta V}{\gamma-1}$ | $nC_{P,m}\Delta T = Q_P$ | $\Delta S = nC_{P,m}\ln(T_2/T_1)$; horizontal on $PV$; shallower on $TS$ ($T/C_P$). |
| **Isothermal** (Reversible) | $T = \mathrm{const}$ ($\Delta T = 0$) | $P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2$ | $nRT\ln(V_2/V_1) = nRT\ln(P_1/P_2)$ | $0$ | $W_{\mathrm{by}} = nRT\ln(V_2/V_1)$ | $0$ | $\Delta S = Q/T = nR\ln(V_2/V_1)$; hyperbola on $PV$; horizontal on $TS$. |
| **Adiabatic** (Isentropic) | $Q = 0$ ($\Delta S = 0$) | $PV^\gamma = \mathrm{c.}$, $TV^{\gamma-1} = \mathrm{c.}$ | $-\Delta U = \frac{P_1V_1 - P_2V_2}{\gamma-1}$ | $nC_{V,m}\Delta T$ | $0$ | $nC_{P,m}\Delta T = \gamma\Delta U$ | $\Delta S = 0$ (rev.); steeper than isotherm on $PV$ ($-\gamma P/V$); vertical on $TS$. |
| **Polytropic** ($n_{\mathrm{p}} \ne 1$) | $PV^n = \mathrm{const}$ | $TV^{n-1} = \mathrm{const}$ | $\frac{P_1V_1 - P_2V_2}{n - 1} = \frac{n_{\mathrm{mol}}R(T_1 - T_2)}{n - 1}$ | $n_{\mathrm{mol}}C_{V,m}\Delta T$ | $n_{\mathrm{mol}}C_n\Delta T$ | $n_{\mathrm{mol}}C_{P,m}\Delta T$ | $C_n = C_V\frac{n-\gamma}{n-1}$; $\Delta S = n_{\mathrm{mol}}C_n\ln(T_2/T_1)$; unifies $n \in \{0, 1, \gamma, \infty\}$. |
| **Free Exp.** (Vacuum) | $Q = 0$, $P_{\mathrm{ext}} = 0$ | $T_1 = T_2$ (IG), $P_1V_1 = P_2V_2$ | $0$ (unresisted expansion) | $0$ (IG) | $0$ | $0$ (IG) | $\Delta S_{\mathrm{sys}} = \Delta S_{\mathrm{univ}} = +nR\ln(V_2/V_1) > 0$ (**irrev.** adiabat; `E2 MC6, E3 MC1`). |
| **Throttling** (J–T Plug) | Adiabatic porous plug | $H_1 = H_2$ ($\Delta H = 0$) | Flow work $P_1V_1 - P_2V_2 = U_2 - U_1$ | $U_2 - U_1$ ($0$ for IG) | $0$ | $0$ (**isenthalpic**) | $\Delta S_{\mathrm{IG}} = +nR\ln(P_1/P_2) > 0$; cools if $\mu_{\mathrm{JT}} = (\partial T/\partial P)_H > 0$ (`E2 MC7`). |

}{**Table:** Master Comparison Flash Card of the 7 Named Power & Refrigeration Cycles (`Rule 5.c.iv`; tested on `E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, E6, E7, E8`)  **[S13,S25,S26,S30]**.

| **Cycle Name** | **Four Constituent Legs ($1\to 2\to 3\to 4\to 1$)** | **Heat In ($Q_H$) & Out ($Q_C$) Legs** | **Efficiency $\eta$ / COP & Non-Standard Coordinate Cues** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Carnot** (Reversible Limit) | $1\to 2$: Isothermal exp. ($T_H$); $2\to 3$: Adiabatic exp. ($T_H\to T_C$); $3\to 4$: Isothermal comp. ($T_C$); $4\to 1$: Adiabatic comp. ($T_C\to T_H$). | $Q_H = nRT_H\ln(V_2/V_1)$ ($1\to 2$); $Q_C = nRT_C\ln(V_3/V_4)$ ($3\to 4$); adiabats force $V_2/V_1 = V_3/V_4$. | $\eta_C = 1 - \frac{T_C}{T_H}$ ($T$ in $K$!). **Rectangle on $T$–$S$ diagram** ($W_{\mathrm{net}} = (T_H-T_C)\Delta S$, `E4 Q12`). On **$P$–$T$ diagram** (`E2 P2b`), isotherms are vertical lines and adiabats follow $P \propto T^{\gamma/(\gamma-1)}$ ($W$ requires knowing $n$!). |
| **2. Stirling** (Regenerative) | $1\to 2$: Isothermal exp. ($T_H, V_1\to V_2$); $2\to 3$: Isochoric cooling ($V_2$); $3\to 4$: Isothermal comp. ($T_C, V_2\to V_1$); $4\to 1$: Isochoric heating ($V_1$). | $W_{\mathrm{net}} = nR(T_H - T_C)\ln(V_2/V_1)$. Internal regenerator transfers $Q_{\mathrm{regen}} = nC_{V,m}(T_H - T_C)$ between $2\to 3$ and $4\to 1$. | **With ideal regenerator:** $\eta_{\mathrm{Stirling,ideal}} = 1 - \frac{T_C}{T_H} = \eta_C$. **Without regenerator (`E6 Sec IV`):** $Q_{\mathrm{in}} = nRT_H\ln(V_2/V_1) + nC_{V,m}(T_H - T_C)$, so $\eta_{\mathrm{no-regen}} = W_{\mathrm{net}}/Q_{\mathrm{in}} < \eta_C$! |
| **3. Ericsson** (Regenerative) | $1\to 2$: Isothermal exp. ($T_H$); $2\to 3$: Isobaric cooling ($P_2$); $3\to 4$: Isothermal comp. ($T_C$); $4\to 1$: Isobaric heating ($P_1$). | Isobaric regenerator transfers $Q_{\mathrm{regen}} = nC_{P,m}(T_H - T_C)$ internally between $2\to 3$ and $4\to 1$. | With ideal regenerator: $\eta_{\mathrm{Ericsson,ideal}} = 1 - \frac{T_C}{T_H} = \eta_C$. Notice Ericsson uses **2 isotherms + 2 isobars** (whereas Stirling uses 2 isotherms + 2 isochores; `E1 Q18`). |
| **4. Otto** (Gasoline Spark) | $1\to 2$: Adiabatic comp. ($V_1\to V_2$); $2\to 3$: Isochoric heat add ($V_2$); $3\to 4$: Adiabatic exp. ($V_2\to V_1$); $4\to 1$: Isochoric heat rej. ($V_1$). | $Q_H = nC_{V,m}(T_3 - T_2)$ ($2\to 3$); $Q_C = nC_{V,m}(T_4 - T_1)$ ($4\to 1$). | $\eta_{\mathrm{Otto}} = 1 - \frac{1}{r^{\gamma-1}} = 1 - \frac{T_1}{T_2}$, where compression ratio $r = V_1/V_2$ (`E6` formula sheet). Higher $r$ and higher $\gamma$ increase efficiency. |
| **5. Diesel** (Compression Ign.) | $1\to 2$: Adiabatic comp. ($r = V_1/V_2$); $2\to 3$: **Isobaric** heat add ($r_c = V_3/V_2$); $3\to 4$: Adiabatic exp.; $4\to 1$: Isochoric heat rej. ($V_1$). | $Q_H = nC_{P,m}(T_3 - T_2)$ ($2\to 3$, constant $P$); $Q_C = nC_{V,m}(T_4 - T_1)$ ($4\to 1$, constant $V$). | $\eta_{\mathrm{Diesel}} = 1 - \frac{1}{r^{\gamma-1}}\left[\frac{r_c^\gamma - 1}{\gamma(r_c - 1)}\right]$. Because bracket $>1$ for $r_c > 1$, $\eta_{\mathrm{Diesel}} < \eta_{\mathrm{Otto}}$ at the same $r$, but Diesel engines operate at higher $r$ ($15\text{--}22$ vs. $9\text{--}12$) without knock. |
| **6. Brayton** (Gas Turbine / Jet) | $1\to 2$: Adiabatic comp. ($P_1\to P_2$); $2\to 3$: Isobaric heat add ($P_2$); $3\to 4$: Adiabatic exp. ($P_2\to P_1$); $4\to 1$: Isobaric heat rej. ($P_1$). | $Q_H = nC_{P,m}(T_3 - T_2)$ ($2\to 3$); $Q_C = nC_{P,m}(T_4 - T_1)$ ($4\to 1$). | $\eta_{\mathrm{Brayton}} = 1 - \frac{1}{r_p^{(\gamma-1)/\gamma}} = 1 - \frac{T_1}{T_2}$, where pressure ratio $r_p = P_2/P_1$. Consists of **2 adiabats + 2 isobars**. |
| **7. Rankine** (Steam Power Plant) | $1\to 2$: Adiabatic turbine exp. (boiler $P_{\mathrm{high}} \to$ condenser $P_{\mathrm{low}}$); $2\to 3$: Isobaric/isothermal condenser ($x_2 \to$ sat. liq. $3$); $3\to 4$: Adiabatic pump; $4\to 1$: Isobaric boiler. | $q_{\mathrm{in}} = h_1 - h_4$ (boiler); $q_{\mathrm{out}} = h_2 - h_3$ (condenser); $w_t = h_1 - h_2$; $w_p = h_4 - h_3 \approx v_{f,3}(P_{\mathrm{high}}-P_{\mathrm{low}})$. | **Cornell 2027 `E1 Q18, Q28–29` Focus:** Ideal turbine is isentropic ($s_{2s} = s_1 \implies x_{2s} = (s_1 - s_{f,\mathrm{low}})/s_{fg,\mathrm{low}}$, $h_{2s} = h_{f,\mathrm{low}} + x_{2s}h_{fg,\mathrm{low}}$). Real work: $w_{t,a} = \eta_s(h_1 - h_{2s})$; $s_{\mathrm{gen}} = s_{2a} - s_1$; $X_{\mathrm{dest}} = T_0 s_{\mathrm{gen}}$. |

}### [FORMULA & DECISION CARD: Cycle Coordinate Translator: How the 4 Canonical Processes Appear on $P$–$V$, $T$–$S$, and $P$–$T$ Plots]

| **Process** | **On $P$–$V$ Diagram ($\text{Area} = \int P\,dV = W_{\mathrm{by}}$)** | **On $T$–$S$ Diagram ($\text{Area} = \int T\,dS = Q_{\mathrm{rev}}$)** | **On $P$–$T$ Diagram (`E2 P2b`)** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Isochoric** ($V=\mathrm{const}$) | **Vertical straight line** ($\Delta V = 0 \implies W_{\mathrm{by}} = 0$) | Curve with positive slope $(\partial T/\partial S)_V = T/C_V$ (steeper than isobar) | Straight line through origin: $P = (nR/V)T$ |
| **Isobaric** ($P=\mathrm{const}$) | **Horizontal straight line** ($W_{\mathrm{by}} = P\Delta V$) | Curve with positive slope $(\partial T/\partial S)_P = T/C_P$ (shallower than isochor) | **Horizontal straight line** ($P = \mathrm{const}$) |
| **Isothermal** ($T=\mathrm{const}$) | Rectangular hyperbola $P \propto V^{-1}$ (slope $-P/V$) | **Horizontal straight line** ($Q_{\mathrm{rev}} = T\Delta S$) | **Vertical straight line** ($T = \mathrm{const}$) |
| **Adiabatic / Isentropic** | Steep curve $P \propto V^{-\gamma}$ (slope $-\gamma P/V$, $\gamma\times$ steeper than isotherm) | **Vertical straight line** ($\Delta S = 0 \implies Q_{\mathrm{rev}} = 0$) | Curve $P \propto T^{\gamma/(\gamma-1)}$; on $\ln P$ vs. $\ln T$, slope $= \frac{\gamma}{\gamma-1} = \frac{C_{P,m}}{R} = \frac{C_{V,m}+R}{R}$! |

}### [2027 HEAT-COLLECTOR DEVICE & LAB: 2027 Heat-Lamp Collector Physics & Optical/Thermal Design Summary (`Rules 3–6` & `Clarifications #1–#9`)]
- **Lamp Spectrum & Aperture Concentration:** A $100–125 W$ incandescent heat-lamp tungsten filament ($T_{\mathrm{fil}} \approx 2300–2450 K$) peaks at $\lambda_{\max} = 2897.8 µm K / 2400 K = \mathbf{1.21 µm}$ (near-IR) and emits $\approx 82\%\text{--}86\%$ of its electrical power as radiation. Funneling the full allowed $29.6 cm \times 29.6 cm$ top aperture ($A_{\mathrm{ap}} = 876 cm^2$) down onto the $7.5 cm$ mouth of the 9 oz clear plastic cup ($A_{\mathrm{cup}} = 44.2 cm^2$) via a specular shiny-side aluminum foil compound reflector ($\rho_{\mathrm{NIR,spec}} = 0.88\text{--}0.91$ shiny side vs. $0.58\text{--}0.68$ dull side!) provides a geometric concentration potential of $C_{\mathrm{geom}} = 876 / 44.2 = \mathbf{19.8\times}$  **[S12,S19]**.
- **Near-IR Water Surface Absorption & Stable Stratification (`Clarifications #1–#4`):** From Hale & Querry (1973) and Kou et al. (1993)  **[S19,S20]**, liquid water's absorption coefficient jumps from $\mu_a(1.0 µm) = 0.36 /cm$ to $\mu_a(1.45 µm) = 28.8 /cm$ ($\delta_p = 0.35 mm$) and $\mu_a(1.95 µm) = 114 /cm$ ($\delta_p = 0.088 mm$). Thus **$>68\%$ of absorbed lamp power is deposited directly into the top $10 mm$ water layer**. Because warmer water above $4 °C$ is less dense than cooler water below it ($\partial\rho/\partial z > 0, \mathrm{Ra} < 0$), natural convection is completely suppressed! Under `Clarifications #1–#4` (zero stirring/swirling; ES measures top water layer near cup center)  **[S02]**, this stratified top layer ($C_{\mathrm{top,eff}} \approx 215 J/K$ vs. bulk $418.4 J/K$) boosts measured $\mathrm{TG}$ by **$1.5\times\text{--}1.9\times$** over a mixed cup.
- **Why Non-Attached Glazing (`Clarification #5`) Saves $3.5–7.0 °C$:** As proved in Lienhard Example 11.11 (pp. 662–664)  **[S12]**, evaporative mass transfer from an uncovered $40 °C$ water cup ($\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{evap}} \approx 2.22 W$, $L_v = 2406 kJ/kg$) accounts for **$73\%\text{--}82\%$ of all top-surface heat loss** and cools the exact top skin the ES thermometer measures! Resting a non-attached clear BoPET film window ($\tau_{\mathrm{NIR}} = 0.90$, no tape/adhesives/clips on the cup per `Clarification #5`) traps saturated $100\%\ \mathrm{RH}$ air above the cup and eliminates evaporative loss.

## Top-15 Exam-Day Point-Losing Traps & Rapid Cram Verification Drills

{**Table:** Top-15 Point-Losing Exam Traps & 5-Second Diagnostic Fixes Synthesized from `E1–E8` Official Rubrics  **[S25,S26,S27,S28,S29,S30,S31,S32]**.

| **#** | **Trap / Wrong Move** | **What It Produces / Why It Fails on Rubrics** | **5-Second Diagnostic & Fix** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **T01** | Using gauge pressure $P_{\mathrm{gauge}}$ in $PV=nRT$ or steam tables (`E1 Q27c, Q28`) | Underestimates $P_{\mathrm{abs}}$ by $101.3 kPa$, ruining $v_g$, $h = u + Pv$, and all 8 steam-table cells (`TB #1`). | Circle “gauge” in problem text $\implies$ immediately write $P_{\mathrm{abs}} = P_{\mathrm{gauge}} + 101.3 kPa$! |
| **T02** | Multiplying/dividing by $T$ in °C instead of K (`E8 Q26`) | Gives $27^\circ\mathrm{C} \times 8/7 = 30.9 °C$ (distractor `c`) instead of $300.15 K \times 8/7 = 343.0 K = 69.9 °C$. | Convert **every** single-state temperature to Kelvin before touching $PV=nRT, \eta_C, \Delta S$, or $\sigma T^4$. |
| **T03** | Adding $+273.15$ or $+32$ to a temperature *difference* $\Delta T$ (`E7 Q5, E8 Q5`) | Turns $\Delta T = 100 °C$ into $373 K$ (distractor `d`) instead of $\Delta T = 100 K = 180\ ^\circ\mathrm{F}$. | Check for $\Delta$ or $/K$: intervals scale by slope only ($1\text{ C}^\circ = 1\text{ K} = 1.8\text{ F}^\circ = 1.8\text{ R}^\circ$). |
| **T04** | Assuming all ice melts or all steam condenses without checking plateau (`E1 Q30d, E4 Q9a`) | Predicts impossible $T_f < 0 °C$ or $T_f > 100 °C$ when the mixture actually stops at $T_f = T_{\mathrm{melt}}$ or $T_{\mathrm{boil}}$. | Always compute $E_{\mathrm{net},0}$ relative to $0 °C$ liquid water first (`[C08]` 5-Zone Ledger). |
| **T05** | Using $L_v(100 °C) = 40.68 kJ/mol$ for evaporation at $T < 100 °C$ (`E2 P3e TB#3`) | Loses 6 of 9 rubric points on MIT 2019 `P3e` ($L_v$ at $37 °C$ is $43.3 kJ/mol = 2413 kJ/kg$, not $2257$!). | When $C_{P,l}$ and $C_{P,g}$ are given for sub-boiling evaporation, apply Kirchhoff shift `[C10]`. |
| **T06** | Confusing Heat Capacity $C$ $[J/K]$ with Specific Heat $c$ $[J/kg/K]$ (`E1 Q5,17a`) | Misclassifies Heat Capacity $C = mc$ as intensive (`E1 Q5`) instead of **extensive**; or omits mass $m$. | “Specific” or “molar” $=$ Intensive; bare “Heat Capacity” $C$ $=$ Extensive! |
| **T07** | Omitting calorimeter $C_{\mathrm{cal}}$ or glass bulb expansion $\beta_g V_0 \Delta T$ (`E1 Q26d, E7 Q16`) | Underestimates total heat $Q = (m_w c_w + C_{\mathrm{cal}})\Delta T$ by $54\%$ on `E7 Q16` (distractor `b`)! | Always check whether vessel $C_{\mathrm{cal}}$ or $\beta_{\mathrm{glass}}$ is given in the problem header. |
| **T08** | Flipping First-Law work sign $W_{\mathrm{by}}$ vs. $w_{\mathrm{on}}$ (`E4 Q13`: $-2 pts$/subpart) | Subtracts instead of adds $Q = \Delta U + W_{\mathrm{by}}$ during gas expansion ($\Delta V > 0$). | Expansion ($\Delta V > 0$) ALWAYS has $W_{\mathrm{by}} > 0$ ($w_{\mathrm{on}} < 0$) and $\Delta U = Q - W_{\mathrm{by}}$. |
| **T09** | Confusing exitance $M = \sigma T^4$ with Lambertian radiance $L = \sigma T^4/\pi$ (`E1 Q36e TB#2`) | Overestimates directional radiance $L$ $[W/m^2/sr]$ by a factor of $\pi = 3.1416$! | Check units: $W/m^2$ $=$ exitance $M = \sigma T^4$; $W/m^2/sr$ $=$ radiance $L = \sigma T^4/\pi$. |
| **T10** | Averaging $\gamma_i$ directly in a gas mixture or using $M$ in $g/mol$ in $v_{\mathrm{rms}}$ | $M$ in $g/mol$ makes $v_{\mathrm{rms}} = \sqrt{3RT/M}$ too small by $\sqrt{1000} = 31.6\times$! | Always put $M$ in $kg/mol$ ($\mathrm{O_2} = 0.032$) and compute $\gamma_{\mathrm{mix}} = C_{P,\mathrm{mix}}/C_{V,\mathrm{mix}}$. |
| **T11** | Using $C_V = \frac{3}{2}Nk_B$ for a 2D crystal lattice (`E1 Q35a TB#3`) | Assumes 2D lattice is $\frac{1}{2}$ of 3D ($3Nk_B$), forgetting each 2D atom has 2 KE + 2 PE $= 4$ modes! | A $d$-dimensional harmonic crystal has $2d$ quadratic modes/atom $\implies C_V = d\cdot Nk_B$ ($2Nk_B$ in 2D). |
| **T12** | Confusing Rayleigh number $\mathrm{Ra}$ with thermal radiation (`E1 Q17e TB#12`) | Marks True on “$\mathrm{Ra}$ determines whether transfer is by radiation or free convection.” | $\mathrm{Ra} = \mathrm{Gr}\cdot\mathrm{Pr}$ compares **buoyancy vs. viscous/thermal diffusion** (conduction vs. convection). |
| **T13** | Leaving units or exact sig figs off final answers (`E1, E2, E4, E6`) | Loses $1.0 pt$ per problem ($25\%\text{--}33\%$ of score) on `E2` MIT and `E4` GGSO rubrics! | In the final 3 minutes, audit every answer box for explicit units and requested sig figs. |
| **T14** | Blind guessing on $+3\text{ correct} / +1\text{ blank} / 0\text{ wrong}$ MCQs (`E2`) | Expected value of 4-choice blind guess is $0.75 pts < 1.00 pt$ blank credit! | When blank credit $= 1/3$ of correct credit, guess **only** after eliminating $\ge 2$ choices (§`sec:21.4`). |
| **T15** | Swirling the 9 oz cup during removal or using `#6 PS` Styrofoam (`2027 Part II`) | Swirling destroys top-layer stratification ($-5\text{ to }-9 °C$ in $\mathrm{TG}$!); `#6 PS` disqualifies device ($\mathrm{TS}=\mathrm{PS}=0$)! | Lift cup straight up with zero tilt/swirl (`Clarif. #1–4`); purge all `#6 PS` (`Clarif. #6`). |

}### Worked Example — Rapid Cram Drill 1: Eight-Scale Temperature Crossovers `[Rule 5.c.i]`

Prove algebraically the exact temperatures where **(a)** Kelvin and Fahrenheit read the same number ($T_{\mathrm{K}} = T_{\mathrm{F}}$), and **(b)** Celsius and Delisle read the same number ($T_{\mathrm{C}} = T_{\mathrm{De}}$)  **[S25,S27]**.

**Solution.**
**(a)** Substitute $T_{\mathrm{C}} = T_{\mathrm{K}} - 273.15$ into $T_{\mathrm{F}} = 1.8\,T_{\mathrm{C}} + 32$ and set $T_{\mathrm{K}} = T_{\mathrm{F}} = x$: $x = 1.8(x - 273.15) + 32 \implies 0.8x = 459.67 \implies x = \mathbf{574.5875\text{ K} = 574.5875\ ^\circ\mathrm{F}}$.
**(b)** Set $T_{\mathrm{C}} = T_{\mathrm{De}} = y$ in $T_{\mathrm{De}} = 150 - 1.5\,T_{\mathrm{C}}$: $y = 150 - 1.5y \implies 2.5y = 150 \implies y = \mathbf{+60.0\ ^\circ\mathrm{C} = +60.0\ ^\circ\mathrm{De}}$.

**✓ Verified by:** Independent Python script `check_sec21_23.py` (`SEC23_SCALE_INTERSECTIONS`): $x = 574.5875$, $y = 60.0$.

### Worked Example — Rapid Cram Drill 2: Open-Cup Evaporation Loss vs. BoPET Glazing Cap `[Clarification #5]`

During a 10-minute 2027 collector run, an uncovered 9 oz cup holding 100 mL ($100.0 g$) of water at mean surface temperature $40.0 °C$ ($L_v = 2406 J/g$) loses $\Delta m_{\mathrm{evap}} = 0.550 g$ of water by evaporation  **[S12]**. How many degrees Celsius of temperature gain $\mathrm{TG}$ are lost from **(a)** the ES-measured top stratified layer ($C_{\mathrm{top,eff}} = 215.0 J/K$), and **(b)** the bulk water ($C_{\mathrm{bulk}} = 418.4 J/K$)?

**Solution.**
The latent heat removed directly from the water surface skin by evaporating $0.550 g$ is $Q_{\mathrm{evap}} = \Delta m_{\mathrm{evap}}\,L_v = (0.550 g)(2406 J/g) = \mathbf{1323.3 J}$.
**(a) Top stratified layer loss:** $\Delta T_{\mathrm{top,lost}} = Q_{\mathrm{evap}}/C_{\mathrm{top,eff}} = 1323.3 J / 215.0 J/K = \mathbf{6.155 °C}$ (**6.2 °C saved by a non-attached BoPET cap!**).
**(b) Bulk-averaged loss:** $\Delta T_{\mathrm{bulk,lost}} = Q_{\mathrm{evap}}/C_{\mathrm{bulk}} = 1323.3 J / 418.4 J/K = \mathbf{3.163 °C}$.

**✓ Verified by:** Independent Python script `check_sec21_23.py` (`SEC23_EVAPORATION_PENALTY_DRILL`): $Q_{\mathrm{evap}} = 1323.3 J$, $\Delta T_{\mathrm{top}} = 6.155 °C$.

### Worked Example — Rapid Cram Drill 3: Rankine First-Law vs. Second-Law Exergy Efficiency `[Cornell 2027 E1 Q29]`

In Cornell 2027 (`E1 Q29`)  **[S25]**, a Rankine steam cycle absorbs $q_{\mathrm{in}} = 2257.19 kJ/kg$ in a boiler heated by a furnace at $T_{\mathrm{source}} = 600 K$ (ambient dead state $T_0 = 300 K$) and produces net turbine work $w_{\mathrm{net}} = 109.92 kJ/kg$. Compute **(a)** the First-Law thermal efficiency $\eta_1$, **(b)** the supplied exergy $X_{\mathrm{in}}$, and **(c)** the Second-Law exergy efficiency $\eta_2$ (`TB #8`).

**Solution.**
**(a)** First-Law efficiency: $\eta_1 = w_{\mathrm{net}}/q_{\mathrm{in}} = 109.92 / 2257.19 = 0.048698 = \mathbf{4.870\%}$.
**(b)** Maximum reversible (Carnot) work extractable from $q_{\mathrm{in}}$ between $600 K$ and $300 K$ ($\eta_C = 1 - 300/600 = 0.5000$): $X_{\mathrm{in}} = q_{\mathrm{in}}(1 - T_0/T_{\mathrm{source}}) = 2257.19(0.5000) = \mathbf{1128.60 kJ/kg}$.
**(c)** Second-Law efficiency: $\eta_2 = w_{\mathrm{net}}/X_{\mathrm{in}} = \eta_1/\eta_C = 4.8698\% / 50.00\% = \mathbf{9.740\%}$.

**✓ Verified by:** Independent Python script `check_sec21_23.py` (`SEC23_EXERGY_SECOND_LAW_EFF`): $\eta_1 = 4.870\%$, $X_{\mathrm{in}} = 1128.6 kJ/kg$, $\eta_2 = 9.740\%$.

### [FORMULA & DECISION CARD: 60-Second Last-Minute Partner Execution Card (Read Together 2 Minutes Before Block Start)]

** PARTNER A (Lead Theorist: `5.c.ii, iv, vii`)**
- **At $t = 0{:}00$:** Unstaple/split written packet; place detached `QS-01, 03, 04, 06, 07, 08, 14` across desk (Fig. `fig:21:workspace-layout`). Flag all **Tiebreaker (`TB`)** items.
- **At $t = 5{:}30$:** Cross-check Partner B's 15-second $T_{\mathrm{pred}}$ addition on Calculator #1: $T_{\mathrm{pred}} = \mathrm{TG}_{\mathrm{tab}}(h, P, t) + k_{\mathrm{start}}\,T_{\mathrm{start}} + k_{\mathrm{room}}\,T_{\mathrm{room}}$. Confirm $T_{\mathrm{pred}}$ is written in **°C** (never Kelvin!) and handed to ES.
- **Pass 1 & Pass 2 ($t = 2\text{--}38 min$):** Sweep phase diagrams (`QS-04`), 5-zone ice-water-steam calorimetry (`QS-03`), gas laws (`QS-05`), Carnot/Stirling/Rankine cycles (`QS-08`), and $\Delta S/\Delta H/\Delta G$/exergy (`QS-07`).
- **Pass 3 ($t = 38\text{--}47 min$):** Write symbolic governing equations on every remaining Tier 3 subpart + carry-forward values.

- **Minutes $9\text{--}15$ & $17\text{--}47$ ($40 min$ Written Sprint):** Sweep Pile B: 8 temperature scales & energy units (`QS-01`), 8 named scientists (`QS-14`), conduction/convection/Newton heating (`QS-09, 10, 12`), and blackbody Stefan–Boltzmann/Wien (`QS-11`).

## Target-Variable Chooser II: First Law, Entropy, Potentials & Cycles (§7–§9)

| **Target Unknown (SI Unit)** | **Given Knowns / Cue** | **Closed-Form Algebraic Equation** | **Validity / Flags** | **Ref.** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\Delta U$ (J) | Heat $Q$ in, work $W_{\mathrm{by}}$ out (or $w_{\mathrm{on}}$) | $\Delta U = Q - W_{\mathrm{by}} = q + w_{\mathrm{on}}$;\quad Ideal gas: $\Delta U = n C_{V,m}\Delta T = \dfrac{\Delta(PV)}{\gamma - 1}$ | **[CLOSED]** Universal 1st Law | §`sec:07` |
| $\Delta H$ (J) | $\Delta U, \Delta(PV)$ or constant-$P$ heat $Q_P$ | $\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta(PV)$;\quad Ideal gas: $\Delta H = n C_{P,m}\Delta T = \gamma\,\Delta U$ | Closed or steady flow | §`sec:07` |
| $W_{\mathrm{by}}$ (Isobaric, J) | Constant pressure $P$, $\Delta V$ or $\Delta T$ | $W_{\mathrm{by}} = P(V_2 - V_1) = n R(T_2 - T_1)$;\quad $Q_P = n C_{P,m}\Delta T$ | $P = \mathrm{const}$ ($n=0$) | §`sec:07` |
| $W_{\mathrm{by}}$ (Isothermal, J) | Constant $T$, $V_1, V_2$ (or $P_1, P_2$) | $W_{\mathrm{by}} = Q_T = n R T \ln\!\left(\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}\right) = P_1 V_1 \ln\!\left(\dfrac{P_1}{P_2}\right)$;\quad $\Delta U = 0$ | **[IDEAL-GAS]** **[REV]** ($n=1$) | §`sec:07` |
| $W_{\mathrm{by}}$ (Adiabatic, J) | $Q = 0$, $P_1,V_1,P_2,V_2$ or $T_1,T_2$ | $W_{\mathrm{by}} = -\Delta U = -n C_{V,m}(T_2 - T_1) = \dfrac{P_1 V_1 - P_2 V_2}{\gamma - 1}$ | **[IDEAL-GAS]** **[REV]** ($PV^\gamma = \mathrm{C}$) | §`sec:07` |
| $T_2, P_2, V_2$ (Adiabatic) | Initial $(P_1,V_1,T_1)$, $\gamma = C_P/C_V$ | $P_1 V_1^\gamma = P_2 V_2^\gamma$;\quad $T_1 V_1^{\gamma-1} = T_2 V_2^{\gamma-1}$;\quad $T_1^\gamma P_1^{1-\gamma} = T_2^\gamma P_2^{1-\gamma}$ | **[IDEAL-GAS]** **[REV]** **[CONST-c]** | §`sec:07` |
| $W_{\mathrm{by}}, Q$ (Polytropic, J) | $PV^n = \mathrm{const}$ ($n \ne 1$) | $W_{\mathrm{by}} = \dfrac{P_1 V_1 - P_2 V_2}{n - 1} = \dfrac{nR(T_1 - T_2)}{n - 1}$;\quad $Q = n C_{V,m}\!\left(\dfrac{n - \gamma}{n - 1}\right)\!\Delta T$ | **[IDEAL-GAS]** **[REV]** Polytropic | §`sec:07` |
| $W_{\mathrm{by}}$ (Irreversible Step) | Sudden expansion against fixed $P_{\mathrm{ext}}$ | $W_{\mathrm{by}} = P_{\mathrm{ext}}(V_2 - V_1)$ (if adiabatic: $n C_{V,m}\Delta T = -P_{\mathrm{ext}}\Delta V$) | Irreversible step | §`sec:07` |
| $\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{cv}} - \dot{W}_{\mathrm{sh}}$ (Steady Flow) | Control volume inlet $1 \to$ exit $2$ | $\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{cv}} - \dot{W}_{\mathrm{sh}} = \dot{m}\Big[(h_2 - h_1) + \tfrac{1}{2}(u_2^2 - u_1^2) + g(z_2 - z_1)\Big]$ | **[STEADY-FLOW]** SFEE | §`sec:07` |
| $\mu_{\mathrm{JT}}$ (K/Pa) | Throttling valve ($h_2 = h_1$) | $\mu_{\mathrm{JT}} = \left(\dfrac{\partial T}{\partial P}\right)_H = \dfrac{1}{C_P}\!\left[T\left(\dfrac{\partial V}{\partial T}\right)_P - V\right] \approx \dfrac{2a/(RT) - b}{C_{P,m}}$ | $\mu_{\mathrm{JT}}=0$ for **[IDEAL-GAS]** | §`sec:07` |
| $\Delta S_{\mathrm{trs}}$ (J/K) | Phase transition at constant $T_{\mathrm{trs}}, P$ | $\Delta S_{\mathrm{trs}} = \dfrac{\Delta H_{\mathrm{trs}}}{T_{\mathrm{trs}}} = \dfrac{\pm m L}{T_{\mathrm{trs}}}$ ($T_{\mathrm{trs}}$ in K!) | **[STATE/NAT]** Reversible phase chg | §`sec:08` |
| $\Delta S_{\mathrm{solid/liq}}$ (J/K) | Constant-$c$ body heated $T_1 \to T_2$ | $\Delta S = m c \ln\!\left(\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}\right) = n C_m \ln\!\left(\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}\right)$ | **[STATE/NAT]** **[CONST-c]** Incomp. | §`sec:08` |
| $\Delta S_{\mathrm{IG}}$ (J/K) | Ideal gas $(T_1,V_1,P_1) \to (T_2,V_2,P_2)$ | $\Delta S = n C_{V,m}\ln\dfrac{T_2}{T_1} + nR\ln\dfrac{V_2}{V_1} = n C_{P,m}\ln\dfrac{T_2}{T_1} - nR\ln\dfrac{P_2}{P_1}$ | **[STATE/NAT]** **[IDEAL-GAS]** **[CONST-c]** | §`sec:08` |
| $\Delta S_{\mathrm{mix}}$ (J/K) | Distinct ideal gases mixed at $T, P$ | $\Delta S_{\mathrm{mix}} = -R\sum_{i} n_i \ln x_i > 0$ ($x_i = n_i/n_{\mathrm{tot}}$) | **[STATE/NAT]** **[IDEAL-GAS]** Distinct species | §`sec:08` |
| $S_{\mathrm{Boltzmann}}$ (J/K) | Microstate multiplicity $\Omega$ | $S = k_B \ln\Omega$;\quad $\Delta S = k_B \ln(\Omega_2/\Omega_1)$ | Statistical mechanics | §`sec:08` |
| $\Delta_{\mathrm{rxn}}H^\circ, \Delta_{\mathrm{rxn}}S^\circ$ | Standard formation tables (Table `app:A.4`) | $\Delta_{\mathrm{rxn}}H^\circ = \sum \nu_p \Delta_f H_p^\circ - \sum \nu_r \Delta_f H_r^\circ$; $\Delta_{\mathrm{rxn}}S^\circ = \sum \nu_p S_p^\circ - \sum \nu_r S_r^\circ$ | **[STATE/NAT]** Hess's law | §`sec:08` |
| $\Delta H^\circ(T_2), \Delta S^\circ(T_2)$ | $\Delta C_P = \sum \nu_p C_{P,p} - \sum \nu_r C_{P,r}$ | $\Delta H^\circ(T_2) = \Delta H^\circ(T_1) + \Delta C_P(T_2 - T_1)$; $\Delta S^\circ(T_2) = \Delta S^\circ(T_1) + \Delta C_P\ln\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}$ | **[STATE/NAT]** Kirchhoff's law | §`sec:08` |
| $\Delta G, K_{\mathrm{eq}}$ | $\Delta H, \Delta S$, reaction quotient $Q_r$ | $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S = \Delta G^\circ + RT\ln Q_r$;\quad $\Delta G^\circ = -RT\ln K_{\mathrm{eq}}$ | **[STATE/NAT]** Fixed $T, P$ | §`sec:08` |
| $X_{\mathrm{dest}}, W_{\mathrm{rev,max}}$ (J) | Dead state $T_0$, entropy gen. $S_{\mathrm{gen}}$ | $X_{\mathrm{dest}} = W_{\mathrm{lost}} = T_0 S_{\mathrm{gen}} = T_0\Delta S_{\mathrm{univ}} \ge 0$ | **[STATE/NAT]** Gouy–Stodola | §`sec:08` |
| $T_{f,\mathrm{rev}}, W_{\max}$ (2 Finite Bodies) | Identical $C_1 = C_2 = C$ at $T_{1,i}, T_{2,i}$ | $T_{f,\mathrm{rev}} = \sqrt{T_{1,i}T_{2,i}}$;\quad $W_{\max} = C\big(T_{1,i} + T_{2,i} - 2\sqrt{T_{1,i}T_{2,i}}\big)$ | Reversible Carnot extraction | §`sec:08` |
| $\eta_{\mathrm{th}}, \eta_{\mathrm{Carnot}}$ | Heat engine $Q_H, Q_C, W_{\mathrm{net}}, T_H, T_C$ | $\eta_{\mathrm{th}} = \dfrac{W_{\mathrm{net}}}{Q_H} = 1 - \dfrac{Q_C}{Q_H} \le \eta_C = 1 - \dfrac{T_C}{T_H}$ | $T_H, T_C$ in K! | §`sec:09` |
| $\mathrm{COP}_R, \mathrm{COP}_{\mathrm{HP}}$ | Refrigerator / heat pump $Q_C, Q_H, W_{\mathrm{in}}$ | $\mathrm{COP}_R = \dfrac{Q_C}{W_{\mathrm{in}}} \le \dfrac{T_C}{T_H - T_C}$;\quad $\mathrm{COP}_{\mathrm{HP}} = \dfrac{Q_H}{W_{\mathrm{in}}} = \mathrm{COP}_R + 1 \le \dfrac{T_H}{T_H - T_C}$ | $T_H, T_C$ in K! | §`sec:09` |
| $\eta_{\mathrm{Otto}}, \eta_{\mathrm{Diesel}}, \eta_{\mathrm{Brayton}}$ | Compression $r$, cutoff $r_c$, pressure $r_p$ | $\eta_{\mathrm{Otto}} = 1 - r^{1-\gamma}$; $\eta_{\mathrm{Diesel}} = 1 - r^{1-\gamma}\dfrac{r_c^\gamma - 1}{\gamma(r_c - 1)}$; $\eta_{\mathrm{Brayton}} = 1 - r_p^{(1-\gamma)/\gamma}$ | Air-standard **[IDEAL-GAS]** **[CONST-c]** | §`sec:09` |

| $\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{cond}}, R_{\mathrm{slab}}$ (W, K/W) | Plane slab $k, A, L, \Delta T$ | $\dot{Q} = \dfrac{k A (T_1 - T_2)}{L} = \dfrac{T_1 - T_2}{R_{\mathrm{slab}}}$,\quad $R_{\mathrm{slab}} = \dfrac{L}{kA}$,\quad $R_{\mathrm{val}} = \dfrac{L}{k}$ | 1D Steady conduction | §`sec:10` |

| $R_{\mathrm{tot}}, T_k$ (Interface Temp) | Series layers $R_i$ or parallel branches | $R_{\mathrm{ser}} = \sum R_i$;\quad $R_{\mathrm{par}}^{-1} = \sum R_i^{-1}$;\quad $T_k = T_{\mathrm{in}} - \dot{Q}\sum_{i=1}^k R_i$ | Steady thermal network | §`sec:10` |
| $r_{\mathrm{crit,cyl}}, r_{\mathrm{crit,sph}}$ (m) | Insulation $k$, external $h_{\mathrm{ext}}$ | $r_{\mathrm{crit,cyl}} = \dfrac{k}{h_{\mathrm{ext}}}$;\quad $r_{\mathrm{crit,sph}} = \dfrac{2k}{h_{\mathrm{ext}}}$ | Max heat loss at $r_o = r_{\mathrm{crit}}$ | §`sec:10` |
| $\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{fin}}, \eta_f$ (W, $1$) | Perimeter $P$, area $A_c$, length $L_c$ | $m = \sqrt{\dfrac{hP}{kA_c}}$;\quad $\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{fin}} = \sqrt{hPkA_c}(T_b-T_\infty)\tanh(mL_c)$;\quad $\eta_f = \dfrac{\tanh(mL_c)}{mL_c}$ | 1D Uniform-area fin | §`sec:10` |
| $\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{conv}}, h$ (W, W/m^2/K) | Nusselt $\overline{\mathrm{Nu}}_L$, fluid $k_f$, length $L$ | $h = \dfrac{k_f}{L}\overline{\mathrm{Nu}}_L$;\quad $\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{conv}} = h A(T_s - T_\infty)$;\quad $R_{\mathrm{conv}} = \dfrac{1}{hA}$ | Convection boundary | §`sec:11` |
| $\mathrm{Re}_L, \mathrm{Pr}, \mathrm{Gr}_L, \mathrm{Ra}_L$ | Fluid $\nu, \alpha, \beta$, speed $u_\infty$, $\Delta T$ | $\mathrm{Re}_L = \dfrac{u_\infty L}{\nu}$,\quad $\mathrm{Pr} = \dfrac{\nu}{\alpha} = \dfrac{c_p\mu}{k_f}$,\quad $\mathrm{Gr}_L = \dfrac{g\beta\Delta T L^3}{\nu^2}$,\quad $\mathrm{Ra}_L = \mathrm{Gr}_L\mathrm{Pr}$ | Props at $T_f = \tfrac{1}{2}(T_s+T_\infty)$ | §`sec:11` |
| $\delta_{\mathrm{opt}}$ (Air Gap, m) | Enclosed air layer $\Delta T, \nu, \alpha, \beta$ | Set $\mathrm{Ra}_\delta = \dfrac{g\beta\Delta T \delta^3}{\nu\alpha} \approx 1708 \implies \delta_{\mathrm{opt}} = \left(\dfrac{1708\,\nu\alpha}{g\beta\Delta T}\right)^{1/3} \approx 10–13 mm$ | Suppresses cellular conv. | §`sec:11` |
| $\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{evap}}$ (W) | Open water surface $T_w, \mathrm{RH}, h_{\mathrm{conv}}$ | $\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{evap}} = h_m A L_v\big(\rho_{v,\mathrm{sat}}(T_w) - \mathrm{RH}\cdot\rho_{v,\mathrm{sat}}(T_\infty)\big)$, $h_m \approx \dfrac{h_{\mathrm{conv}}}{\rho_a c_{p,a}\mathrm{Le}^{2/3}}$ | Uncovered water cup | §`sec:11` |
| $\lambda_{\max}$ (m), $M_b$ (W/m^2) | Blackbody temperature $T$ (K) | $\lambda_{\max} = \dfrac{2897.772 µm K}{T}$;\quad $M_b = \sigma T^4 = \pi I_b$ | **[STATE/NAT]** Blackbody radiation | §`sec:12` |
| $\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{rad}}, h_r$ (W, W/m^2/K) | Small surface $\varepsilon, A, T_1$ in room $T_2$ | $\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{rad}} = \varepsilon\sigma A(T_1^4 - T_2^4) \approx h_r A(T_1 - T_2)$,\quad $h_r = 4\varepsilon\sigma\overline{T}^3$ | $T_1, T_2, \overline{T}$ in K! | §`sec:12` |
| $\dot{Q}_{12}$ ($N$ Shields, W) | Parallel plates $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2$, $N$ shields $\varepsilon_s$ | $\dot{Q}_{12} = \dfrac{\sigma A(T_1^4 - T_2^4)}{(1/\varepsilon_1 + 1/\varepsilon_2 - 1) + N(2/\varepsilon_s - 1)} = \dfrac{\dot{Q}_{12,0}}{N+1}$ (if all $\varepsilon$ equal) | Diffuse-gray shields | §`sec:12` |
| $\mathrm{Bi}, \mathrm{Fo}, \tau$ ($1, 1, s$) | Body volume $V$, area $A_s$, $L_c = V/A_s$ | $\mathrm{Bi} = \dfrac{h L_c}{k_s} < 0.1$;\quad $\mathrm{Fo} = \dfrac{\alpha t}{L_c^2}$;\quad $\tau = R_{\mathrm{th}}C_{\mathrm{eff}} = \dfrac{\rho V c_p}{h A_s}$;\quad $\dfrac{t}{\tau} = \mathrm{Bi}\cdot\mathrm{Fo}$ | **[Bi<0.1]** Lumped transient | §`sec:13` |
| $T(t)$ (2027 Lamp Heating, °C) | Absorbed $P_{\mathrm{abs}}$, loss $G_{\mathrm{loss}} = 1/R_{\mathrm{th}}$ | $T(t) = T_{\mathrm{ss}} - (T_{\mathrm{ss}} - T_i)e^{-t/\tau}$,\quad $T_{\mathrm{ss}} = T_\infty + \dfrac{P_{\mathrm{abs}}}{G_{\mathrm{loss}}}$,\quad $\tau = \dfrac{C_{\mathrm{eff}}}{G_{\mathrm{loss}}}$ | 2027 Collector ODE | §`sec:13` |
| $T_{\mathrm{ss}}, \tau$ from 3 Equal Steps | $T_1(t_0), T_2(t_0+\Delta t), T_3(t_0+2\Delta t)$ | $T_{\mathrm{ss}} = \dfrac{T_2^2 - T_1 T_3}{2T_2 - T_1 - T_3}$;\quad $e^{-\Delta t/\tau} = \dfrac{T_3 - T_2}{T_2 - T_1}$;\quad $\tau = \dfrac{\Delta t}{\ln[(T_2-T_1)/(T_3-T_2)]}$ | Equal time steps $\Delta t$ | §`sec:16` |
| $\delta_{\mathrm{th}}$ (m), $T_{\mathrm{contact}}$ | Diffusivity $\alpha$, effusivity $b = \sqrt{k\rho c_p}$ | $\delta_{\mathrm{th}}(t) \approx 2\sqrt{\alpha t}$;\quad $T_{\mathrm{contact}} = \dfrac{b_1 T_{1,i} + b_2 T_{2,i}}{b_1 + b_2}$ | Semi-infinite solids | §`sec:13` |
| $\mathrm{TG}, \mathrm{PE}, \mathrm{FS}$ (2027 Scoring) | $T_i, T_f, T_{\mathrm{pred}}$ (all in $^\circ\mathrm{C}$!) | $\mathrm{TG} = T_f - T_i$; $\mathrm{PE} = 1 - \dfrac{\|T_f - T_{\mathrm{pred}}\|}{T_f}$; $\mathrm{FS} = \mathrm{ES} + \mathrm{TS} + \mathrm{PS}$ | **[2027-RULE]** 6.a–j ($0.7^{N_{\mathrm{c}}}0.9^{N_{\mathrm{p}}}$) | §`sec:16` |
| $R(T)$ (Pt100 RTD / NTC) | $R_0 = 100 Ω$ at $0^\circ\mathrm{C}$; Steinhart–Hart $\beta$ | RTD: $R(T) = R_0(1 + \alpha_{\mathrm{Pt}}T_C)$ ($\alpha_{\mathrm{Pt}}=3.85×10^{-3}/^\circ\mathrm{C}$); NTC: $R(T) = R_0 e^{\beta(1/T - 1/T_0)}$ | Thermometry sensors | §`sec:17` |
| $u_c(y)$ (GUM Uncertainty) | Independent inputs $x_i \pm u(x_i)$ | Sum $y=\sum c_i x_i \Rightarrow u_c^2 = \sum c_i^2 u^2(x_i)$; Product $y=\prod x_i^{p_i} \Rightarrow \left(\dfrac{u_c}{y}\right)^2 = \sum p_i^2\!\left(\dfrac{u(x_i)}{x_i}\right)^2$ | JCGM 100 GUM **[S21]** | §`sec:17` |

# Appendix C: Master Symbol Dictionary, Glossary & Printed 5-Index Suite {#app:C}

> **[SCOPE: REQUIRED | Locked Notation Contract (§2) + 5 Auto-Generated MakeIndex Retrieval Indices]**

## Master Thermodynamic, Heat-Transfer & 2027 Collector Symbol Dictionary

| **Symbol** | **Quantity Name** | **SI Unit** | **Critical Disambiguation & Sign / Context Rules** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $Q$ vs. $\dot{Q}$ vs. $q''$ | Heat energy vs. heat rate vs. heat flux | J; W; W/m^2 | $Q > 0$ enters system (J); $\dot{Q} = dQ/dt$ is power (W); $q'' = \dot{Q}/A$ is flux (W/m^2); $q = Q/m$ is specific heat transfer (J/kg). |
| $W_{\mathrm{by}}$ vs. $w_{\mathrm{on}}$ | Boundary work by vs. on system | J | Physics (locked): $\Delta U = Q - W_{\mathrm{by}}$ ($W_{\mathrm{by}} = +\int P\,dV > 0$ expansion). Chemistry: $\Delta U = q + w_{\mathrm{on}}$ ($w_{\mathrm{on}} = -W_{\mathrm{by}} > 0$ compression). |
| $U, H, F, G$ | Internal energy, enthalpy, Helmholtz, Gibbs | J | Extensive state functions ($H = U + PV$, $F = U - TS$, $G = H - TS$). Lowercase $u, h, f, g$ are mass-specific (J/kg); $U_m, H_m, G_m$ are molar (J/mol). |
| $S, s, S_m, S_{\mathrm{gen}}$ | Entropy (total, specific, molar, generated) | J/K; J/kg/K; J/mol/K | State function ($dS = \delta Q_{\mathrm{rev}}/T$); $S_{\mathrm{gen}} = \Delta S_{\mathrm{univ}} = \Delta S_{\mathrm{sys}} + \Delta S_{\mathrm{surr}} \ge 0$ ($=0$ iff reversible). |
| $c, c_p, c_v$ vs. $C$ vs. $C_m$ | Specific vs. total vs. molar heat capacity | J/kg/K; J/K; J/mol/K | $C = m c = n C_m$ (J/K) is extensive object/calorimeter capacity; $c$ is per unit mass; $C_{P,m}, C_{V,m}$ are per mole. |
| $L_f, L_v, L_s$ | Specific latent heats (fusion, vap., subl.) | J/kg (or kJ/kg) | Molar forms: $\Delta H_{\mathrm{fus},m} = M L_f$, $\Delta H_{\mathrm{vap},m} = M L_v$, $\Delta H_{\mathrm{sub},m} = M L_s$ (J/mol). |
| $R$ vs. $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$ vs. $R_{\mathrm{th}}$ vs. $R_{\mathrm{val}}$ | Gas const. vs. specific gas const. vs. thermal resistance vs. $R$-value | J/mol/K; J/kg/K; K/W; m^2 K/W | $R = 8.31446 J/mol/K$; $R_{\mathrm{sp}} = R/M$; $R_{\mathrm{th}} = \Delta T/\dot{Q} = L/(kA)$ (K/W); $R_{\mathrm{val}} = A R_{\mathrm{th}} = L/k$ (m^2 K/W). |
| $h$ vs. $h_{\mathrm{conv}}$ vs. $h_c$ vs. $h_{\mathrm{Planck}}$ | Specific enthalpy vs. convection coeff. vs. contact conductance vs. Planck const. | J/kg; W/m^2/K; W/m^2/K; J s | Check units: enthalpy $h = u + Pv$ (J/kg or kJ/kg); heat transfer $h, h_c, h_r$ (W/m^2/K); $h_{\mathrm{bulb}}$ is lamp bulb height ($40–65 cm$). |
| $k$ vs. $k_B$ | Thermal conductivity vs. Boltzmann const. | W/m/K; J/K | Always write Boltzmann constant with subscript $k_B = 1.380649×10^{-23} J/K$. |
| $\alpha$ vs. $\alpha_L$ vs. $\alpha_{\mathrm{NIR}}$ | Thermal diffusivity vs. linear expansion vs. radiative absorptance | m^2/s; /K; $1$ | $\alpha = k/(\rho c_p)$ (m^2/s); $\alpha_L = L_0^{-1}(dL/dT)$ (/K); $\alpha_\lambda \in [0,1]$ (dimensionless absorptance). |
| $\beta$ vs. $\kappa_T$ vs. $K_T$ | Volumetric expansion, isothermal compressibility, bulk modulus | /K; /Pa; Pa | $\beta = V^{-1}(\partial V/\partial T)_P$ ($\approx 3\alpha_L$ solid, $1/T$ ideal gas); $\kappa_T = -V^{-1}(\partial V/\partial P)_T = 1/K_T$; $C_P - C_V = TV\beta^2/\kappa_T$. |
| $\gamma$ vs. $n$ vs. $f$ | Heat capacity ratio, polytropic index, active DOF | $1$ (dimensionless) | Ideal gas: $\gamma = C_{P,m}/C_{V,m} = (f+2)/f$; polytropic $PV^n = \mathrm{const}$ ($n=0$ isobar, $1$ isotherm, $\gamma$ adiabat, $\infty$ isochore). |
| $\varepsilon, \rho_{\mathrm{opt}}, \tau_{\mathrm{opt}}$ | Emissivity, reflectance, transmittance | $1$ (dimensionless) | Radiation balance: $\alpha + \rho_{\mathrm{opt}} + \tau_{\mathrm{opt}} = 1$; Kirchhoff: $\varepsilon_\lambda(T) = \alpha_\lambda(T)$ at same $\lambda, T$. |
| $M_b, I_b, J, G, F_{ij}$ | Radiant exitance, radiance, radiosity, irradiation, view factor | W/m^2; W/m^2/sr; W/m^2; W/m^2; $1$ | $M_b = \sigma T^4 = \pi I_b$; radiosity $J_i = \varepsilon_i M_{b,i} + (1-\varepsilon_i)G_i$; reciprocity $A_i F_{ij} = A_j F_{ji}$; enclosure $\sum_j F_{ij} = 1$. |
| $\tau$ vs. $\tau_p$ vs. $b$ | Collector time const., probe time const., thermal effusivity | s; s; J/m^2/K/s^1/2 | Collector $\tau = R_{\mathrm{th}}C_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx 900–1400 s$; probe $\tau_p \approx 2–15 s$; effusivity $b = \sqrt{k\rho c_p}$ governs contact temp $T_i$. |
| $\mu_{\mathrm{JT}}$ vs. $Z$ vs. $\omega$ | Joule–Thomson coeff., compressibility factor, humidity ratio / acentric factor | K/Pa; $1$; $\mathrm{kg_v/kg_{da}}$ | $\mu_{\mathrm{JT}} = (\partial T/\partial P)_H = C_P^{-1}(T(\partial V/\partial T)_P - V)$; $Z = PV/(nRT)$; psychrometric $\omega = 0.62198 P_v/(P-P_v)$. |
| $x$ vs. $w_i$ vs. $x_i$ | Vapor quality vs. mass fraction vs. mole fraction | $1$ (dimensionless) | Two-phase quality $x = m_g/(m_f+m_g) \in [0,1]$; alloy mass fraction $w_i = m_i/m_{\mathrm{tot}}$; gas mole fraction $x_i = n_i/n_{\mathrm{tot}}$. |
| $\eta_{\mathrm{th}}, \eta_C, \eta_{\mathrm{II}}, \mathrm{COP}_R, \mathrm{COP}_{\mathrm{HP}}$ | Thermal, Carnot, 2nd-law efficiencies & coefficients of performance | $1$ (dimensionless) | $\eta_{\mathrm{th}} = W_{\mathrm{net}}/Q_H \le \eta_C = 1 - T_C/T_H$; $\eta_{\mathrm{II}} = \eta_{\mathrm{th}}/\eta_C = \mathrm{COP}/\mathrm{COP}_C$; $\mathrm{COP}_{\mathrm{HP}} = \mathrm{COP}_R + 1$. |
| $\mathrm{FS, ES, TS, PS, TG, PE}$ | 2027 Official Scoring Quantities (**[2027-RULE]** 6) | points or $^\circ\mathrm{C}$ | $\mathrm{FS} = \mathrm{ES}_{50} + \mathrm{TS}_{30} + \mathrm{PS}_{20}$; $\mathrm{TG} = T_f - T_i$ ($^\circ\mathrm{C}$); $\mathrm{PE} = 1 - \|T_f - T_{\mathrm{pred}}\|/T_f$ ($T_f$ in $^\circ\mathrm{C}$!). |

| **Group** | **Definition** | **Characteristic Length $L$ or $L_c$** | **Physical Ratio & Competition Threshold Criterion** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Biot $\mathrm{Bi}$ | $h L_c / k_{\mathrm{solid}}$ | $L_c = V/A_s$ ($L$ half-slab, $R/2$ cyl., $R/3$ sph.) | Internal conduction resistance / external convection resistance; $\mathbf{\mathrm{Bi} < 0.10}$ validates lumped capacitance. |

| Reynolds $\mathrm{Re}_L$ | $\rho u_\infty L / \mu = u_\infty L / \nu$ | Plate length $L$ or pipe hydraulic $D_h = 4A_c/P_w$ | Inertia / viscous forces (flat plate transition $\mathrm{Re}_x \approx 5×10^{5}$; internal pipe transition $\mathrm{Re}_D \approx 2300$). |
| Prandtl $\mathrm{Pr}$ | $\nu / \alpha_f = c_p \mu / k_{\mathrm{fluid}}$ | Fluid property (no length scale) | Momentum diffusivity / thermal diffusivity ($\mathrm{Pr}_{\mathrm{air}} \approx 0.71$; $\mathrm{Pr}_{\mathrm{water,25^\circ C}} \approx 6.14$; liquid metals $\ll 0.03$). |
| Grashof $\mathrm{Gr}_L$ | $g\beta\Delta T L^3 / \nu^2$ | Vertical height $L$, horizontal $L = A_s/P$, gap $\delta$ | Buoyancy force $\times$ inertia / $(\text{viscous force})^2$; for ideal gas, evaluate $\beta = 1/T_f$ in Kelvin at film temp $T_f$. |
| Rayleigh $\mathrm{Ra}_L$ | $\mathrm{Gr}_L \mathrm{Pr} = g\beta\Delta T L^3 / (\nu\alpha_f)$ | Vertical wall $L$, horizontal plate $A_s/P$, gap $\delta$ | Buoyancy-driven natural convection parameter (horizontal cavity onset $\mathrm{Ra}_\delta = 1708$; vertical turbulent $\mathrm{Ra}_L > 10^9$). |

## Comprehensive Thermodynamics & 2027 Device Glossary (A–Z)

{- **Absolute zero ($0 K = -273.15 °C$):**  Lower bound of thermodynamic temperature where classical kinetic energy vanishes and crystal entropy reaches its Third-Law floor ($S \to 0$).
- **Acentric factor ($\omega$):**  Pitzer non-sphericity metric $\omega = -\log_{10}(P_{\mathrm{sat}}/P_c)_{T_r=0.7} - 1.0$ measuring departure from simple spherical-molecule corresponding states.
- **Adiabatic process / wall:**  Process or boundary with zero heat transfer ($Q = 0$); a reversible adiabatic process is *isentropic* ($\Delta S = 0$, $PV^\gamma = \mathrm{const}$ for ideal gas).
- **Amagat's law of additive volumes:**  Total volume of an ideal-gas mixture at $(T,P)$ equals the sum of component partial volumes $V_i = x_i V$.
- **Antoine equation:**  Empirical 3-parameter vapor-pressure correlation $\log_{10} P_{\mathrm{sat}} = A - B/(T + C)$ derived from Clausius–Clapeyron.
- **Available energy (Exergy, $X$):**  Maximum useful work obtainable as a system comes into equilibrium with the ambient dead state $(T_0, P_0)$; destroyed exergy is $X_{\mathrm{dest}} = T_0 S_{\mathrm{gen}} \ge 0$.
- **Avogadro's law:**  Equal volumes of all ideal gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules ($V/n = RT/P$).
- **Biot number ($\mathrm{Bi} = hL_c/k_s$):**  Ratio of internal solid conduction resistance to external boundary convection resistance; $\mathrm{Bi} < 0.1$ validates lumped-capacitance $T(t)$.
- **Blackbody:**  Idealized perfect absorber ($\alpha_\lambda = 1$) and emitter ($\varepsilon_\lambda = 1$) at all wavelengths and directions ($M_b = \sigma T^4$).
- **BoPET selective glazing (Mylar):**  Biaxially oriented polyethylene terephthalate film with high near-IR transmittance ($\tau_{\mathrm{NIR}} \approx 0.90$) used as an unattached cup vapor barrier (`Clarification #5`).
- **Boyle temperature ($T_B$):**  Temperature where the second virial coefficient vanishes ($B(T_B) = 0$, so $Z \approx 1$ as $P\to 0$; for a van der Waals gas, $T_B = a/(Rb) = \tfrac{27}{8}T_c$).
- **Calorimeter constant ($C_{\mathrm{cal}}$):**  Effective heat capacity ($J/K$) of the calorimeter cup, stirrer, and thermometer probe assembly ($Q_{\mathrm{cal}} = C_{\mathrm{cal}}\Delta T$).
- **Carnot theorem & efficiency:**  No heat engine operating between $T_H$ and $T_C$ can exceed $\eta_C = 1 - T_C/T_H$ (K), and all reversible engines between $T_H, T_C$ have $\eta = \eta_C$.
- **Choked / critical insulation radius ($r_{\mathrm{crit}}$):**  Outer insulation radius $r_{\mathrm{crit}} = k_{\mathrm{ins}}/h_{\mathrm{ext}}$ (cylinder) or $2k_{\mathrm{ins}}/h_{\mathrm{ext}}$ (sphere) that maximizes heat loss.
- **Clausius inequality:**  $\oint \delta Q/T_b \le 0$ for any cycle, with equality iff totally reversible; implies $dS \ge \delta Q/T$.
- **Clausius–Clapeyron equation:**  Phase-boundary slope $dP/dT = L/(T\Delta v) \approx P\Delta H_{\mathrm{vap},m}/(RT^2)$ when $v_g \gg v_f$ and vapor behaves as an ideal gas.
- **Coefficient of performance ($\mathrm{COP}$):**  Ratio of desired heat transfer to work input: $\mathrm{COP}_R = Q_C/W_{\mathrm{in}}$ (cooling) and $\mathrm{COP}_{\mathrm{HP}} = Q_H/W_{\mathrm{in}} = \mathrm{COP}_R + 1$ (heating).
- **Colligative properties:**  Solution properties ($\Delta T_b = i K_b m$, $\Delta T_f = -i K_f m$, osmotic pressure $\Pi = i M R T$) that depend on total solute particle concentration $i m$.
- **Compressibility factor ($Z = PV/nRT$):**  Measure of non-ideality ($Z=1$ ideal gas; $Z<1$ attractive forces dominate; $Z>1$ repulsive excluded volume $b$ dominates; $Z_c = 3/8 = 0.375$ for vdW gas).
- **Compound parabolic concentrator (CPC):**  Non-imaging reflector profile achieving the thermodynamic sine-law concentration limit $C_{\max} = 1/\sin^2\theta_a$ (3D) without tracking.
- **Contact conductance ($h_c$):**  Interfacial conductance $h_c = q''/\Delta T_{\mathrm{interface}}$ across micro-asperities between mating solids ($R_{\mathrm{contact}} = 1/(h_c A)$).
- **Critical point ($T_c, P_c, V_{m,c}$):**  Terminus of the liquid–vapor coexistence curve where liquid and vapor phases become indistinguishable ($\Delta H_{\mathrm{vap}} \to 0$).
- **Curzon–Ahlborn efficiency ($\eta_{\mathrm{CA}}$):**  Efficiency $\eta_{\mathrm{CA}} = 1 - \sqrt{T_C/T_H}$ of an endoreversible heat engine operating at maximum power output under finite-rate heat transfer.
- **Dalton's law of partial pressures:**  Total pressure of an ideal-gas mixture equals the sum of component partial pressures $P_i = x_i P$.
- **Dead-air gap ($\delta_c \approx 11 mm$):**  Enclosed air space thin enough ($\mathrm{Ra}_\delta < 1708$, $\delta \lesssim 11 mm$) that buoyancy cannot initiate convection cells, so $\mathrm{Nu}_\delta = 1$.
- **Debye $T^3$ law & Dulong–Petit limit:**  Lattice heat capacity approaches $C_{V,m} \to 3R = 24.94 J/mol/K$ per mole of atoms for $T \gtrsim \Theta_D$, and falls as $C_{V,m} \propto (T/\Theta_D)^3$ as $T \to 0\,K$.
- **Delisle scale ($^\circ\mathrm{De}$):**  Historical *inverted* scale ($0\,^\circ\mathrm{De}$ at $100 °C$ steam point, $150\,^\circ\mathrm{De}$ at $0 °C$ ice point): $T_{\mathrm{De}} = 150 - 1.5\,T_C$.
- **Dew-point temperature ($T_{\mathrm{dp}}$):**  Temperature at which moist air cooled at constant pressure and humidity ratio reaches saturation ($P_v = P_{\mathrm{sat}}(T_{\mathrm{dp}})$).
- **Diathermal wall:**  Boundary that permits heat transfer without mass transfer; two systems separated by a diathermal wall reach thermal equilibrium ($T_A = T_B$).
- **Eutectic point ($T_E, w_E$):**  Minimum-melting invariant point ($F=0$ at fixed $P$) in a binary system where liquid transforms isothermally into two solid phases ($L \rightleftharpoons \alpha + \beta$).
- **Extensive vs. intensive properties:**  Extensive quantities ($U, H, S, G, V, m, n, C$) scale linearly with system size; intensive quantities ($T, P, \rho, c, v, \mu_i$) are size-independent. The ratio of any two extensive properties is intensive!
- **Fin efficiency ($\eta_f$) & effectiveness ($\varepsilon_f$):**  $\eta_f = \dot{Q}_{\mathrm{fin}}/\dot{Q}_{\max} = \tanh(mL_c)/(mL_c)$ compares actual fin heat transfer to an isothermal fin at base temp $T_b$; $\varepsilon_f = \dot{Q}_{\mathrm{fin}}/(h A_c \Delta T_b)$ must exceed $2$ to justify fins.
- **Fourier's law of conduction:**  Conductive heat flux vector $\mathbf{q}'' = -k\nabla T$ (W/m^2) is proportional to the negative temperature gradient.
- **Gibbs phase rule ($F = C - P + 2$):**  Number of independent intensive variables $F$ for $C$ chemically independent components across $P$ coexisting phases in equilibrium ($F = C - P + 1$ at fixed pressure).
- **Gibbs paradox:**  Classical distinguishable-particle formula predicts $\Delta S = 2nR\ln 2 > 0$ when mixing two identical gases at $(T,P)$; resolved by quantum indistinguishability ($1/N!$), giving $\Delta S = 0$.
- **Gray vs. selective surface:**  A gray surface has wavelength-independent $\alpha = \varepsilon$; a selective absorber has high near-IR absorptance ($\alpha_{\mathrm{NIR}} \gtrsim 0.90$) and low thermal-IR emissivity ($\varepsilon_{\mathrm{MIR}} \lesssim 0.15$).
- **Heat-engine sign & orientation rule:**  Clockwise closed loop on $P$–$V$ or $T$–$S$ has $W_{\mathrm{net}} = \oint P\,dV = \oint T\,dS > 0$ (power cycle); counterclockwise loop has $W_{\mathrm{net}} < 0$ (refrigerator / heat pump).
- **Inversion temperature ($T_{\mathrm{inv}}$):**  Locus where $\mu_{\mathrm{JT}} = (\partial T/\partial P)_H = 0$ ($T_{\mathrm{inv,max}} = 2a/(Rb) = \tfrac{27}{4}T_c$ for vdW gas). Since $\mathrm{He}$ ($T_{\mathrm{inv}}\approx40 K$) and $\mathrm{H_2}$ ($\approx202 K$) have $T_{\mathrm{inv}} < 300 K$, throttling them at room temperature *warms* them!
- **Kirchhoff's radiation law:**  Spectral directional emissivity equals spectral directional absorptance at the same wavelength and temperature: $\varepsilon_\lambda(T) = \alpha_\lambda(T)$.
- **Lever rule:**  In any binary two-phase region $(\alpha + L)$, the mass fraction of each phase equals the opposite tie-line arm divided by the total tie-line length: $f_L = (w_0 - w_\alpha)/(w_L - w_\alpha)$.
- **Log-mean temperature difference ($\Delta T_{\mathrm{lm}}$):**  Exact mean driving temperature difference in a steady-flow heat exchanger: $\Delta T_{\mathrm{lm}} = (\Delta T_1 - \Delta T_2)/\ln(\Delta T_1/\Delta T_2)$.
- **Lumped-capacitance model:**  Exponential heating/cooling law $\theta(t)/\theta_i = \exp(-t/\tau)$ with $\tau = \rho c_p V/(h A_s) = R_{\mathrm{th}}C$, valid when $\mathrm{Bi} = hL_c/k_s < 0.10$.
- **Maxwell–Boltzmann speed ratios:**  For an ideal gas at temperature $T$, $v_{\mathrm{mp}} = \sqrt{2RT/M} < \bar{v} = \sqrt{8RT/(\pi M)} < v_{\mathrm{rms}} = \sqrt{3RT/M}$ in ratio $1 : 1.1284 : 1.2247$.
- **Polystyrene / #6 PS Disqualification Rule:**  Under 2027 Rule `3.b.i` and `Clarification #6`, ANY polystyrene (expanded EPS Styrofoam, extruded XPS board, or rigid `#6 PS` plastic cup/sheet) triggers immediate **Part II Disqualification**.
- **Prediction Score ($\mathrm{PS}$) Celsius Rule:**  Under 2027 Rule `6.b`, $\mathrm{PE} = 1 - |T_f - T_{\mathrm{pred}}|/T_f$ uses $T_f$ in **degrees Celsius** (never Kelvin!).
- **State vs. path functions:**  State functions ($P, T, V, U, H, S, F, G$) depend only on equilibrium state endpoints ($dU$ exact); path functions ($Q, W_{\mathrm{by}}, S_{\mathrm{gen}}$) depend on process trajectory ($\delta Q, \delta W$ inexact).
- **Thermal stratification in 9 oz cup:**  Stable hot-over-cold density profile formed under top-down lamp heating because near-IR radiation is absorbed in the top $10 mm$ of water while downward buoyancy convection is hydrostatically suppressed.
- **Triple point of water ($273.16 K, 611.657 Pa$):**  Unique invariant state ($F = 1 - 3 + 2 = 0$) where ice Ih, liquid water, and water vapor coexist in equilibrium ($T_{\mathrm{tp}} = 0.01 °C$).

| **`5.II.g–i`** | Lamp OFF; remove cup within $1 min$, **completely separated from all device components**; ES measures $T_f$ to $0.1 °C$. **Clarif. #1–#4:** **Never stir, swirl, or shake water**; ES probes **top water layer near cup center**. | §`sec:00`, §`sec:11`, §`sec:15`, §`sec:16`, §`sec:17`, §`app:D` | Lift cup straight out without sloshing; strip off unattached BoPET cap completely; calibrate §`sec:16` tables for thermally stratified top-center layer ($\kappa_{\mathrm{strat}} \ge 1.25$). | Leaving wrap on cup or swirling water = Comp. Viol. ($\times 0.9$) |
| **`6.a–j`** | High score wins in $°C$: $\mathrm{FS} = \mathrm{ES}(50) + \mathrm{TS}(30) + \mathrm{PS}(20)$, $M_{\mathrm{pen}} = 0.7^{V_c}0.9^{V_p}$, $\mathrm{PE} = 1 - \|T_f-T_{\mathrm{pred}}\|/T_f$. Tiebreakers: **1st Best $\mathrm{TS}$, 2nd Best $\mathrm{ES}$, 3rd test Qs**. | **QS-13**, §`sec:00`, §`sec:16`, §`sec:21` | Verified against Official Scoresheet `v2.0.0` (`11/06/26` **[S04]**). ## Build Pipeline, QA Sign-Off & Selective Duplex Leaf Reprinting

### [FORMULA & DECISION CARD: Rebuilding & Verifying All 4 Production PDFs]

Run from `C: science olympiad Thermodynamics-Binder` using **Python 3.10.4** (`python`, which auto-prepends offline **MiKTeX 25.12** `pdflatex + makeindex`):
- **Build All 4 Targets (`output/*.pdf`):**<br>
    `python build/build.py –target all`<br>
    (*Or* `–target main|gray|quickref|device`)
- **Run Automated Mechanical & Visual QA:**<br>
    `python qa/pdfcheck.py`<br>
    `python verify/verify_all.py`
- **Mandatory Release Gates (`build/pdfcheck-report.md`):**
- **P1:** Exact US Letter ($612.0 \times 792.0\text{ pt}$) on every page.
- **P2:** Main/Gray $\le 280\text{ pp}$; QuickRef $== 12\text{ pp}$.
- **P3:** Zero unresolved cross-reference markers or leaked raw LaTeX macros.
- **P4:** Zero text spans in $0.72\text{ in}$ ($51.84\text{ pt}$) inner 3-hole punch margin.
- **P5–P6:** Footer `Page N of M` + `2026-11-22`; min font $\ge 5.0\text{ pt}$; $100\%$ embedded Type 1 fonts.
    

### [FORMULA & DECISION CARD: Selective Duplex-Safe Page-Pair Replacement]

Because the binder uses `twoside` duplex margins ($0.75\text{ in}$ inner 3-hole punch margin, $0.50\text{ in}$ outer thumb-tab margin), **every physical sheet in the binder is an odd–even duplex leaf pair $(2k-1,\; 2k)$**:
- **Page-Count-Neutral Edits:** Keep edits inside a chapter's final ` clearpage` (or inside a 1-page `quicksheet`) so downstream page numbers do not shift.
- **Identify Physical Leaf Pair $(2k-1,\; 2k)$:**
- Edited **odd page $p=2k-1$** (front/recto) $\Rightarrow$ reprint pages **$p$ to $p+1$**.
- Edited **even page $p=2k$** (back/verso) $\Rightarrow$ reprint pages **$p-1$ to $p$**.
- **Print Settings:** Select **Actual Size / 100%** (never “Fit to Printable Area”), **Two-Sided: Flip on Long Edge**, punch on the $0.75\text{ in}$ inner margin, and swap the single leaf into the 3-ring binder.
